Assume un ruolo speciale nei periodi in cui la Griffin Clocktower chiude per manutenzione: in quelle finestre, le lezioni normalmente ospitate nella torre vengono temporaneamente ricollocate qui, con conseguente sovraffollamento momentaneo dell'edificio.
lexicon.name: Building C

lexicon.content: Building B ospita prevalentemente aule di piccole dimensioni per corsi con iscrizioni limitate e gli uffici del corpo docente. Al piano terra si trova un'area studio comune, aperta a tutti gli studenti, spesso usata per gruppi di studio informali tra una lezione e l'altra.
lexicon.name: Building B

lexicon.content: L'edificio raggruppa sia aule generiche di piccole dimensioni sia lecture theatres più capienti, usate soprattutto per i corsi introduttivi e le classi a maggioranza umana. È il primo punto di contatto con il campus per molte matricole umane, per lo stile architettonico più familiare rispetto agli edifici magici del resto del campus.
lexicon.name: Building A

lexicon.content:
Bluemoon is Blackwood City's nightlife district, a former industrial strip of exposed brick warehouses and converted garages now split between working-class daytime businesses and after-dark venues. By day it's quiet, mechanics, diners, corner bars serving locals. After sundown, neon signage flickers on across the district and it becomes the city's underground entertainment corridor, drawing a mixed crowd of humans and supernaturals alike. Several venues here operate under Neutral Territory status, making Bluemoon one of the few parts of the city where faction politics are expected to stay outside.

[LOCATION INSTRUCTIONS: Daytime scenes here should feel grounded and unglamorous: working-class, practical, low stakes. Nighttime scenes shift to neon-lit, pulsing, slightly hedonistic energy. Always let the tone shift with the hour rather than staying static.]
lexicon.name: Bluemoon

lexicon.content:
The baths stand apart from the Longhouse itself, built of logs thick enough that the walls read as a single piece of wood, set directly over a natural thermal spring. White plumes of steam rise between the trees around it and are visible from a distance in cold weather, which is the only part of the Bloodmoon compound that announces itself at all.

Inside it smells strongly of sulphur and hot water. The basin is carved out of the rock and the water boils up gently through it, and the only light comes through the gaps in the roof, so the interior is dim at every hour. It is the one place in the compound where the old household routine still runs exactly as it always has: someone prepares the baths, and the baths are used, and nobody has changed the procedure in a very long time.
lexicon.name: Bloodmoon Longhouse Baths

lexicon.content:
La massiccia struttura norrena millenaria sotto il grande tasso. Niente elettricità, zero tecnologia. Il dominio assoluto di Wulfnic e dei Firstborn.

Il grande tasso sorge accanto alla sala, non lontano: è l'albero che Wulfnic ha piantato, e ai suoi piedi nasce la sorgente dello Yarrow. Intorno alla radura si stringe un'enclave di capanne norrene, una ventina, dove vive il branco. Legno, torba e pietra, fuochi veri, nessun cavo.

C'è un solo accesso: il sentiero sterrato che sale nei boschi da Villa Douglas. Nessuna strada asfaltata arriva fin qui, e non ce n'è una seconda.
lexicon.name: Bloodmoon Longhouse

lexicon.content: L'ospedale principale di Blackwood City, nel tranquillo distretto residenziale di Arcadia, vicino alle scuole primarie della città.
lexicon.name: Blackwood General Hospital

lexicon.content:
Popular with 'cryptid' and less-common species, the Bigfeet Hiking Club is very welcoming to new members and organises a r ange of hikes and camping trips over the academic year. Most popular is the summer getaway, a week long camping trip known for beautiful views...and lots of drinking.
Location: Unicorn Hall
Schedule: Varies
lexicon.name: Bigfeet Hiking Club

lexicon.content: Quartiere residenziale esclusivo di Los Angeles, enclave di ricchezza e vecchio potere. Ritrovo di celebrità mondane, vampiri dell'alta società e ricchi licantropi.
lexicon.name: Beverly Hills

lexicon.content:
Beta Rho Omega is third down the campus side, tucked between Theta Iota Theta above it and Delta Omicron Epsilon below, and looks across the road at Phi Omicron Chi.

The letters read as BRO and the house leans into it without embarrassment. It is the athletes' house: Jared Thompson, Bailey Rogers and Santiago Herrera all live here, and the split between Bulls and Bears runs straight through the common room, which is either the best thing about the house or the reason nothing gets decided in it.

The front yard has a permanent set of weights under a tarp and a barbecue that has never once been put away. Noise carries north to the TIT, which is the single most reliable source of friction on the Row and has never escalated past shouting from a window.
lexicon.name: Beta Rho Omega (BRO or ΒΡΩ)

lexicon.content:
Beta Epsilon Epsilon is last on the outer side, the southernmost house on the Row, directly opposite Mu Alpha Nu.

Being at the bottom of the street means the longest walk to campus and the least foot traffic past the door, and being opposite MAN means the house shares a stretch of road with the one fraternity that has a political position. Those two facts define the place more than anything the house does on its own.

The letters follow the animal pattern shared with MOO, DOE and FOX.
lexicon.name: Beta Epsilon Epsilon (BEE or ΒΕΕ)

lexicon.content: The broad civic centerpiece of downtown Bakersfield, California. Characterized by wide sunbaked avenues, red-brick municipal halls, classic clock towers, and heat-resistant desert landscaping, the square acts as a prominent Central Valley hub where regional logistics, agricultural commercial interests, and inland supernatural packs intersect.
lexicon.name: Bakersfield Square

lexicon.content: L'edificio ospita sia il dipartimento di Belle Arti, con aule di pittura e scultura sempre disordinate e piene di opere in corso, sia quello di Arti Performative, con sale prova per danza, teatro e musica. Un Auditorium interno viene usato regolarmente per saggi, spettacoli studenteschi e proiezioni.
lexicon.name: Arts Building

lexicon.content:
Artemis is the women's hall at CUMS, a long gothic block on the north side of the campus with heavy shutters on every window and a courtyard that gets no direct sun at any hour, which was the point of building it there.

The hall runs on the university's crepuscular timetable: quiet through the middle of the day, awake from late afternoon, loudest around midnight. Rooms are doubles with blackout fittings as standard rather than as an accommodation, and the lower floor is windowless for residents who want it that way.

About half the hall is at least part vampire, which at CUMS is simply the demographic and not a remark. The rest are fae, undead of various kinds, and a small number of witches admitted on ability.

It is named for the moon, and its residents have opinions about the fact that the men's hall is named for the sun.
lexicon.name: Artemis Dorms

lexicon.content: Motel scadente con annessa tavola calda lungo la Route 101, a metà strada tra Blackwood City e Solarton. Funge da punto di sosta neutrale per viandanti soprannaturali e corrieri: territorio strettamente neutrale, niente spargimenti di sangue.
lexicon.name: Area di Servizio "The Halfway House"

lexicon.content: Una delle scuole primarie del quiet distretto residenziale di Arcadia, a Blackwood City, non lontano dal Blackwood General Hospital.
lexicon.name: Arcadia School

lexicon.content: Quartiere residenziale di Blackwood City, a ridosso di Seven Hills. Case familiari, vita di quartiere tranquilla; ospita il Blackwood General Hospital (principale struttura ospedaliera cittadina) e il polo scolastico low-grade della città (asilo, elementari e medie), a differenza delle strutture accademiche superiori/universitarie che si trovano invece a Solarton (SUCC). Di fatto è annesso al territorio di Seven Hills: non ha un proprio pack leader di distretto e ricade sotto l'autorità dei Seven Hills.
lexicon.name: Arcadia

lexicon.content:
Apollo is the men's hall at CUMS, the south block, built to the same plan as Artemis and to the same specification: shutters, blackout, a windowless lower floor, and a courtyard laid out to stay shaded.

The naming is the university's joke on itself. The sun hall is where nobody wants sun, and every intake works this out in its first week and thinks it is the first to notice.

The hall keeps the campus crepuscular schedule and is the more social of the two residences, which mostly means the courtyard is in use at three in the morning and Artemis has complained about it in writing more than once.

Most of the Clams and the Beavers live here in season, which does not help the noise.
lexicon.name: Apollo Dorms

lexicon.content:
SUCC's Anime Club: An informal group where both human and supernatural otakus gather to watch anime and discuss anime & manga series.
Location: Library Basement Meeting Room 005
Schedule: Fridays at 6 PM
Known Members: Stan Davies Jr., Andrew Campbell, Oskar
lexicon.name: Anime Club

lexicon.content:
Alpha Sigma Sigma is fourth on the outer side, between Phi Omicron Chi and Beta Epsilon Epsilon, looking across at Delta Omicron Epsilon.

The letters spell ASS and the house has spent decades deciding that this is funny rather than a problem, which has shaped the entire personality of the place. The ASS is the party house of record: loudest, least organised, most likely to be the reason campus security drives down the Row on a Friday.

Vincent and Andrew Campbell both live here.

The alternating layout of the Row puts a sorority directly opposite every fraternity, and the ASS has DOE, which means the house's noise problem is a neighbour problem and not an abstraction.
lexicon.name: Alpha Sigma Sigma (ASS or ΑΣΣ)

lexicon.content:
Alpha Rho Omega sits at the very top of the campus side of the Row, first house you reach walking down from the main campus, with Mu Omega Omega directly across the road.

It is the least theatrical of the five fraternities. No columns, no painted letters three feet high, just a wide porch that always has somebody on it and a lawn that gets mowed roughly when somebody remembers. The house reads as a place people live in rather than a place people perform in.

Finnegan Novak lives here. The ARO porch looks straight down onto the Theta Iota Theta front steps, so whoever ends up living in that sorority in a given year is his immediate neighbour and neither of them can leave the house without the possibility of running into the other. Revazhael lives here too, and does the handyman work for the sorority next door, which is less a job than a consequence of geography.

The practical effect of the position is that ARO is the crossing point of the Row. Everyone walking to campus from any of the ten houses passes this porch.
lexicon.name: Alpha Rho Omega (ARO or ΑΡΩ)

lexicon.content: Il viale delle confraternite del SUCC. Strutture imponenti, feste perenni e forte segregazione per clan o specie.
lexicon.name: Fraternity & Sorority Row (Greek Row)

lexicon.content: Edificio amministrativo del SUCC. Uffici burocratici, presidenza, segreterie.
lexicon.name: Administration

lexicon.content: Alloggi extra per studenti del SUCC, appartamenti condivisi appena fuori dal ring principale del campus.
lexicon.name: Additional Student Housing

lexicon.content:
A&Co. has a wide street front on the main Bricklane lane, all mirror and warm light, and the mannequins in the window are not human shaped: one has a ten foot wingspan, one is built for a centaur's barrel, one has four arms.

The sign is three characters and a full stop, black on white, with the ampersand in fuchsia. Nobody who has not met Angelo Moreno reads anything into it. Everybody who has met him reads Angelo and Company and understands that the loud part of the name is the part he could not resist.

It is the Solarton window of Eidolon Creative, not its home. The house is in Blackwood City, in Paradise; this is where the line is actually sold, to the people it was cut for.

What they sell is fit. Jeans and trousers with a tail port, hemmed and reinforced rather than cut open with scissors at home. Shirts and jackets cut for a wingspan, back panels split and fastened so the wings come through without the whole garment hanging like a sack. Collars and hoods sized for ears that do not lie flat. Hats with horn cutouts in every configuration anybody has thought to ask for. Shoes for digitigrade feet and for hooves. Compression wear that does not chafe over scales. Formalwear, which is the expensive end and the reason the place stays open, because a demihuman who needs a suit for a funeral has nowhere else to go.

The staff measure properly, they do not stare, and they have heard the question before. For a lot of young supernaturals the first trip to A&Co. is the first time getting dressed has not been a compromise, and the shop knows perfectly well what it is actually selling, which is not clothes.

The alterations counter at the back does same day work and is where the real business happens.
lexicon.name: A&Co.

lexicon.content: Bricklane Mall e un pittoresco centro commerciale all'aperto situato a breve distanza dal cuore pulsante di Solarton e dal perimetro della SUCC, caratterizzato da bassi edifici in mattoni rossi a due piani affacciati su vicoli pedonali lastricati. Nessun grande franchising e presente: vi sorgono boutique indipendenti, botteghe esoteriche e servizi dedicati a una clientela mista. Tra le attivita piu note spicca Medusa's, il salone di acconciatura piu in voga della contea, rinomato per tagliare, pettinare e curare capigliature di ogni tipo (siano esse composte da capelli umani, chiome serpentine viventi, piume arpie o criniere leonine). Poco distante sorge lo Yeti Shack, un frequentatissimo chiosco specializzato in granite termoregolatrici, ghiaccioli arcani e dolci sottozero progettati per consentire a specie a temperatura corporea elevata di affrontare il caldo estivo. Due cortili alberati alberati con jacarande e panchine in ferro battuto offrono spazio per il relax pomeridiano degli studenti tra una lezione e l'altra.
lexicon.name: Bricklane Mall

lexicon.content:
Every camper arrives through the same timber-and-steel gatehouse whether they come by family car, camp shuttle, medical transfer, or supernatural transport. Intake scanners identify bloodline signatures, curses, Infernal Cores, Grace, unstable transformations, spectral bodies, hidden weapons, active pacts, and dangerous bonds.

The shuttle loop includes covered loading, luggage carts, reinforced seating, wing clearance, miniature Pixie transport compartments, large-form access, aquatic humidity support, and a small emergency medical bay. First-years are usually met by residential staff and a fifth-year from their cabin.

Parents frequently leave faster than their camper expects. Staff are used to anger, relief, tears, awkward goodbyes, and parents who look far too pleased to be driving away.
lexicon.name: Arrival Gate & Shuttle Loop

lexicon.content:
The Girls Residential Zone contains Moonflower, Silver Birch, Foxglove, Blue Heron, Firefly, Willow Glass, Red Clover, and Starling cabins. Path lanterns glow violet after dark. The zone has its own laundry, bathhouse, pavilion, vending alcove, first-aid cabinet, and staffed night office.

The social ecosystem is intense: borrowed clothes, porch conversations, grudges, late-night food runs, cabin alliances, dating drama that has to happen elsewhere, and the occasional entire cabin standing outside because someone filled the bathroom with spectral fog or accidental glamour.

Boys are not permitted inside or immediately around the zone except authorized emergency personnel.
lexicon.name: Girls Residential Zone

lexicon.content:
The Boys Residential Zone contains Ironwood, Black Pine, Cedar Smoke, Raven Rock, Storm Lantern, Northwind, Lake Wolf, and Thorn Maple cabins. Path lanterns glow amber after dark. The zone mirrors the girls' side with laundry, bathhouse, common shelter, vending, first aid, and a night office.

The culture is a messy mix of gaming, sports gear, drying towels, borrowed chargers, improvised music, power arguments, hidden snacks, and campers pretending not to wait for a text back. Older campers teach first-years practical tricks that never appear in orientation.

Girls are not permitted inside or immediately around the zone except authorized emergency personnel.
lexicon.name: Boys Residential Zone

lexicon.content:
Each residential zone has a twenty-four-hour laundry and bathhouse because eighty supernatural young adults produce absurd quantities of ruined clothing. Machines include oversized drums, wing-safe cycles, fur and scale filters, blood pre-rinse, scent-neutral settings, and separate washers for magically contaminated fabric.

Bathhouses add private showers, soaking tubs, grooming counters, wing-rinse bays, claw-safe drains, and locked product storage. Campers may use cabin bathrooms instead.

Maintenance crews repair claw marks, burned drywall, broken doors, flooded rooms, ectoplasm stains, and holes caused by somebody forgetting how heavy they are in a transformed body. Safe maintenance shifts can earn Camp Credit.
lexicon.name: Laundry & Bathhouses

lexicon.content:
The Rec Hall is a wide modern building with two floor-to-ceiling glass walls reinforced by transparent wards. Inside are oversized couches, giant beanbags, charging tables, vending machines, open art shelves, pool, ping-pong, air hockey, foosball, board games, card tables, TVs, consoles, and enough flexible floor space for events.

A central fireplace is real but protected by heat wards. Staff supervise from a distance rather than hovering. The hall stays open late and becomes the default place for friendships, flirting, arguments, tournaments, homework, birthday disasters, and people silently sitting near others because they do not want to be alone.

The Rec Hall is deliberately not a training room.
lexicon.name: Rec Hall (Camp Mystic)
lexicon.comment: 🪟 Rec Hall — Glass, Metal & Giant Beanbags

lexicon.content:
Twelve Quiet Rooms line a side corridor of the Rec Hall. Campers can reserve them for one to three hours. Each has a couch or daybed, dimmable lighting, acoustic insulation, desk, charging outlets, adjustable temperature, privacy glass, weighted blankets, and an emergency call button.

They are used for studying, video calls, decompression, private conversations, reading, crying without an audience, and sensory recovery. Cameras are not used inside. Door and emergency sensors remain active.

Camp Credit can buy priority reservation during busy periods, but medical or accessibility need overrides the queue. Quiet Rooms are not approved feeding or sexual spaces; partner appointments use the medical suites.
lexicon.name: Reservable Quiet Rooms

lexicon.content:
The Computer Lounge contains high-end desktops, printers, secure video booths, drawing tablets, accessible stations, and entertainment VR. Campers use it for online classes, job applications, coding, gaming, art, research, and family calls. Ghosts have conductivity interfaces and Pixies have miniature workstations.

The adjoining Media Lounge holds large TVs, modern and retro consoles, surround sound, movie libraries, tabletop games, and modular seating. The sound system has Banshee-safe limiters and Siren-resonance filters.

Unlike Training District simulators, recreation VR is entertainment only. Nobody is allowed to turn game night into covert power practice.
lexicon.name: Computer & Media Lounges

lexicon.content:
The Art Studio provides paints, clay, sewing machines, printmaking, jewelry tools, digital tablets, scrap materials, safe carving stations, and lockable supernatural-material cabinets. Basic supplies are free; expensive specialty materials can use Camp Credit.

Several soundproof performance rooms support singing, instruments, recording, dance practice, and small rehearsals. Banshees and Sirens can engage safety filters that prevent supernatural resonance from carrying beyond the room.

Nobody grades the art. The studio exists because a camper who only experiences their power through control drills can start believing control is their whole identity.
lexicon.name: Art Studio & Performance Rooms

lexicon.content:
The indoor trampoline park has wall trampolines, foam pits, tumbling lanes, parkour blocks, warped walls, harnesses, and reinforced netting. It is recreational first and training second.

Full-size Dragons, massive Demon forms, heavy Werebeast hybrids, and uncontrolled gravity or force powers use designated sessions. Winged campers can practice low-risk takeoff and landing. Ghosts are forbidden from phasing through foam-pit floors solely to scare people after repeated complaints.

The park is popular because physically intense movement does not have to become combat.
lexicon.name: Trampoline Park

lexicon.content:
The outdoor complex includes two basketball courts, a convertible soccer/football field, a running loop, two tennis courts, and a smaller practice field. Games can be power-free, passive-trait, or fully supernatural depending on the posted rules.

The Sports Shed stores balls, rackets, pads, helmets, goals, life jackets, fishing gear, winter equipment, and adaptive sports gear. Items are signed in and out through camper IDs. Honest breakage is less serious than hiding damaged equipment.

The field has drainage, reinforced turf, and shielded night lighting for light-sensitive campers. Sports are intended as recreation, not another measure of whether someone deserves to be at camp.
lexicon.name: Courts, Fields, Tennis & Sports Shed

lexicon.content:
The aquatic recreation building contains a heated pool, deep lane, shallow social area, accessible ramps, humid recovery room, and large hot tub. It supports winter swimming, rehabilitation, campers who dislike open water, and aquatic species who need regular immersion.

Merfolk can request salt or freshwater adjustment during closed sessions. Sirens, aquatic Beastfolk, and Werecrocodiles use the deep lane when not booked for training.

No high-output water magic, Siren compulsion, underwater possession, blood feeding, or predatory games are allowed during public swim. The hot tub has supernatural temperature controls because fire-aligned campers have already proven why it needs them.
lexicon.name: Indoor Heated Pool & Hot Tub

lexicon.content:
The Administration Lodge handles enrollment, schedules, transportation, legal documents, Camp Credit disputes, family communication, incident reports, discharge planning, and the endless paperwork created by supernatural adults.

It contains the director and deputy offices, residential services, counseling rooms, consent and legal offices, conference spaces, records storage, and a calm reception area. Campers can walk in for routine issues without appointment.

A private side entrance is used by donors and outside medical partners. The Lodge is also where difficult meetings happen: feeding violations, family conflict, early discharge, legal trouble, or a fifth-year admitting they are afraid to leave.
lexicon.name: Administration Lodge

lexicon.content:
The main Training Complex contains configurable rooms designed to survive powers that would destroy ordinary architecture. Walls contain smart materials, runic dampeners, celestial shielding, infernal grounding, sound absorption, fire suppression, water drainage, psychic insulation, and emergency spatial locks.

Before a session, the system loads the camper's power profile and adjusts permitted force, emergency countermeasures, environmental conditions, and recording settings. Staff can simulate hunger distraction, crowds, darkness, confined spaces, open water, bad weather, hostile magic, or sensory overload while preserving emergency exits.

The purpose is not to make campers fearless. It is to let them fail without catastrophe.
lexicon.name: Supernatural Training Complex

lexicon.content:
Camp Mystic's room-scale simulators combine holography, controlled magic, physical platforms, scent, directional sound, and force feedback. They can reproduce city streets, forests, houses, hospitals, nightclubs, schools, storms, crowds, donor emergencies, feeding temptation, supernatural attacks, and rescue scenarios.

A Vampire can practice leaving an injured human untouched. A Dragon can rehearse reversion inside a collapsing building. A Ghost can practice rescue possession without entering a real body. A Siren can train in a simulated crowd where nobody's autonomy is actually at risk.

The simulators are training-only. The Rec District has separate consumer VR for games.
lexicon.name: 3D Simulation Chambers

lexicon.content:
The clinic combines ordinary hospital equipment with supernatural medicine: trauma bays, imaging, surgery, potion storage, healing wards, blood labs, spectral diagnostics, aquatic treatment, wing and tail supports, transformation-safe beds, and private recovery rooms.

A Zombie with cognitive slippage, Ghoul nearing Hollow state, Eros demon in energy starvation, Banshee with Resonance Mesh injury, Dragon in Compression Strain, or Nephilim with Grace Burn is treated medically before anyone asks about discipline.

The clinic connects directly to the Feeding Center and Training Complex through restricted corridors. Emergency care never costs Camp Credit.
lexicon.name: Mystic Medical Clinic

lexicon.content:
The Feeding & Donor Center has separate entrances for campers, staff, living donors, and postmortem tissue deliveries. It contains blood storage, brain and tissue freezers, demon feeding suites, Eros partner rooms, life-force rooms, donor recovery, counseling offices, kitchens, private feeding rooms, and a laboratory that tests incoming donations.

Some rooms look like ordinary medical suites. Others are reinforced for claws, fangs, true forms, strong scent response, or large bodies. Living donor areas have couches, showers, recovery snacks, and independent advocates.

Campers can use a discreet side corridor if they do not want everyone in the Dining Commons knowing they have an appointment.
lexicon.name: Feeding & Donor Center

lexicon.content:
The Containment Hall is a massive reinforced room for practicing emergency shutdowns. Its floor can divide into zones using anti-flight fields, sound dampening, water barriers, soft-force walls, spectral anchors, heat sinks, magic suppression, or transformation limits.

Campers practice how to stop themselves and how to ask others for help. A Werewolf rehearses restraint before ferality. A Gorgon breaks gaze instantly. A Demonkin drops true form under adrenaline. A Banshee practices silence under panic.

Restraints are used only for drills or real emergencies under medical oversight. The camp does not chain people up as a teaching method. Containment is made familiar so needing it does not automatically feel like punishment.
lexicon.name: Containment & Control Hall

lexicon.content:
One enormous building contains a variable-pressure aquatic tank and a separate vertical flight chamber. The aquatic side serves Merfolk, Sirens, aquatic Beastfolk, Werecrocodiles, water magic users, and Dragons with aquatic forms. Salinity, current, pressure, visibility, temperature, and wave conditions can be adjusted.

The flight side has a high ceiling, wind generators, soft-force catch fields, suspended platforms, nets, and holographic obstacles. Angels, Dragons, Pixies, Fairies, and winged Beastfolk practice takeoff, rescue carrying, confined-space flight, and emergency landing.

Both can be booked for supervised conditioning, but their primary purpose is controlled training.
lexicon.name: Aquatic & Flight Training Hall

lexicon.content:
The main dock is a reinforced floating complex with kayak launches, fishing access, rescue ladders, overhead lighting, and a covered center shelter. The boathouse stores canoes, kayaks, paddleboards, small sailboats, rescue craft, wetsuits, life jackets, and adaptive gear.

Merfolk and Sirens have underwater entry points so they do not need to crawl awkwardly onto the dock. Night boating requires permission.

A line of supernatural buoys marks the far boundary. Crossing them triggers alarms. Farther north sits an older closed pier no longer connected to the main dock.
lexicon.name: Main Dock & Boathouse

lexicon.content:
A large stone-ringed fire pit faces semicircular benches and a small performance platform. Friday nights bring music, stories, announcements, food, flirting, arguments carried into the dark, and at least one staff member pretending not to hear every rumor.

The archery range sits farther inland with standard lanes, adaptive bows, supernatural-strength equipment, moving targets, power-free sessions, and powered competitions.

Campers can earn Camp Credit resetting targets, cleaning benches, setting up events, or preparing ordinary firewood. The area gives Camp Mystic the classic summer-camp image it advertises, just with more fangs in the group photos.
lexicon.name: Bonfire Amphitheater & Archery

lexicon.content:
The Fishing Hut has rods, tackle, bait refrigeration, cleaning stations, maps, weather radios, and a porch that becomes a quiet social space even for campers who never fish.

Nearby workshop barns support woodworking, boat repair, leatherwork, safe metalwork, gear maintenance, outdoor skills, and volunteer repairs. Silver, cold iron, anti-Ghost materials, and other race-targeted substances stay locked in staff storage.

A fifth-year Dragon and a first-year Pixie can work on the same boat repair without their power difference mattering much. That is one reason the workshops are popular.
lexicon.name: Fishing Hut, Workshops & Volunteer Yard

lexicon.content:
Moonflower Cabin (G-01) e uno dei cottage residenziali da sei persone situato nella Girls Residential Zone di Camp Mystic, affacciato su una baia riparata del Lago Erie e illuminato da lanterne esterne a luminescenza violetta. Lo chalet in legno di cedro e travi runiche e strutturato su un unico livello con soppalco mansardato, progettato con sei alcove letto semi-private separate da pesanti tendaggi in lino fonoassorbente per garantire privacy e riposo anche a specie con abitudini circadiane opposte. L'ambiente include un salottino comune con camino in pietra, un angolo cottura provvisto di dispensa e doppio frigorifero (con scomparto schermato e sigillato per le razioni ematiche dei donatori e le conserve mediche), e due bagni completi dotati di estrattori d'aria potenziati. Il programma residenziale di Camp Mystic distribuisce appositamente una studentessa per ciascuno dei cinque anni di corso, a cui si aggiunge Alyssa Douglas-Bloodmoon come sesta occupante durante il soggiorno estivo.

Alyssa porta nello chalet una presenza rassicurante, dolce ma autorevole, intrisa del profumo naturale di miele selvatico, pioggia e moonflower. Come studentessa di medicina e guaritrice di branco, Alyssa e diventata rapidamente il punto di riferimento emotivo e sanitario della cabina: gestisce la cassetta di pronto soccorso, prepara tisane lenitive per calmare lo stress somatico e le fluttuazioni sensoriali, e offre ascolto senza giudizio. La sua indole protettiva si armonizza con le diverse nature delle compagne, creando un clima sereno che smussa le inevitabili tensioni tra predatori.

Roster delle compagne di stanza:

Year 1: Avery Lin Calder (Vampiro). 18 anni (nata il 1 gennaio 2008). Esile, bruna, sguardo scuro e penetrante. Trasformata di recente e discendente della stirpe dei Sette Originali, Avery sta affrontando il suo primo anno di adattamento con un misto di riserbo e timore di perdere il controllo della sete. Possiede il dono vampirico della fine lettura emotiva, che le permette di percepire le sottili sfumature interiori di chi le sta intorno: questo la rende diffidente ma anche profondamente legata alla genuina gentilezza di Alyssa, che non percepisce come finta. Avery etichetta meticolosamente ogni suo contenitore personale nel frigo e nella dispensa; Alyssa si assicura che nessuno tocchi le sue sacche di sangue conservato e la supporta nei momenti di stanchezza all'alba.

Year 2: Sofia Mae Rourke (Strega). 19 anni (nata l'8 febbraio 2007). Statura minuta, fisico atletico, capelli ramati rasati ai lati con ciuffo ribelle e occhi ambrati. Spigliata, creativa e dotata di un'ironia caustica che smorza qualsiasi litigio, Sofia e una specialista in barriere, trasmutazione elementale e contromagie. Riempie la sua alcova di candele d'argilla, gessetti runici e tomi spiegazzati. Sofia e Alyssa trascorrono lunghe serate a confrontare l'erboristeria magica con la farmacologia clinica, e Sofia usa spesso piccoli trucchi pirotecnici innocui per far sorridere le compagne dopo giornate di duro allenamento.

Year 3: Nadia Elise Voss (Licantropo). 20 anni (nata il 4 marzo 2006). Corporatura morbida e robusta, chioma biondo cenere e occhi dorati. Nadia appartiene alla famiglia Voss ed e imparentata con la direttrice Mara Voss. Tranquilla, leale e dotata di una forte empatia di branco, Nadia comprende d'istinto la natura lupina di Alyssa, verso la quale nutre un rispetto spontaneo privo di servilismo. Nadia e la compagna con cui Alyssa condivide le corse mattutine lungo il perimetro boschivo e la gestione dei turni di pulizia della cabina, garantendo stabilita quando la luna piena altera l'umore delle residenti.

Year 4: Talia June Mercer (Donna-Orso / Werebear). 21 anni (nata l'11 aprile 2005). Pelle scura, spalle forti, fisico compatto e atletico, sorella di Theo Mercer (alloggiato nella Ironwood Cabin con Jasper). Talia e la roccia dello chalet: dotata di una forza fisica colossale e di un potere di ancoraggio cinetico, ha un carattere schietto, silenzioso e profondamente protettivo. Non ama i fronzoli e parla poco, ma quando una discussione rischia di degenerare le basta un sospiro profondo o uno sguardo severo per ristabilire l'ordine. In Alyssa riconosce una coetanea seria e responsabile su cui poter sempre contare.

Year 5: Mina Rae Sato (Catwere Beastwere). 22 anni (nata il 7 maggio 2004). Flessuosa, agile come una ballerina, capelli castani ondulati e occhi grigio-argento. Mina e un Beastwere felino: il suo corpo originario e permanente e quello di un grande felino selvatico, mentre la forma umanoide e una costruzione magica temporanea. Essendo al quinto e ultimo anno, Mina e la veterana della Moonflower Cabin: conosce ogni sentiero della riserva, ogni scorciatoia e il programma dei custodi, guidando le compagne piu giovani con consigli pratici e un atteggiamento sornione e rilassato. Adora appollaiarsi sul parapetto della veranda al tramonto e apprezza la quiete che Alyssa sa mantenere nello spazio comune.

La convivenza nella Moonflower Cabin e regolata da un'intesa tacita e affiatata. I turni del bagno tengono conto dei ritmi circadiani opposti tra il sonno diurno di Avery e le sveglie all'alba dei licantropi e degli shifters. La ventilazione magica e i filtri agli ioni curati da Sofia neutralizzano i picchi feromonici durante i cicli lunari, mentre la cucina comune e il teatro di merende serali a base di pasticcini al miele di moonflower e tisane preparate da Alyssa.
lexicon.name: G-01 Moonflower Cabin: Compagne di Stanza di Alyssa
lexicon.comment: 🛖 G-01 Moonflower Cabin: Compagne di Stanza di Alyssa

lexicon.content:
Silver Birch Cabin (G-02) is one of the five-person cabins in the Girls Residential Zone. Camp Mystic deliberately mixes program years so each cabin contains one first-year through one fifth-year rather than isolating newcomers together.

 Year 1: Verena Ivy Novak , Demonkin
 Year 2: Rhea Marie Duvall , Succubus
 Year 3: Imani Claire Hart , Angel
 Year 4: Freya Noelle Kessler , Kresnik
 Year 5: Lena Rose Ortega , Ghoul

The fifth-year is expected to model camp navigation and basic routines, not act as unpaid staff. Cabinmates share a living room, kitchenette, bathrooms, refrigerator, chores, and enough proximity to learn exactly which habits annoy one another. The cabin can become family-like, hostile, competitive, protective, or simply practical depending on who is having a good week.
lexicon.name: G-02 Silver Birch Cabin (Girls Zone)
lexicon.comment: 🛖 G-02 Silver Birch Cabin — Built-In Roster

lexicon.content:
Ironwood Cabin (B-01) e uno dei principali lodge residenziali da sei persone della Boys Residential Zone di Camp Mystic, situato su un promontorio roccioso circondato da pini neri e affacciato sulla riva settentrionale del lago, illuminato da lanterne esterne a luminescenza ambrata. Costruito con massicci tronchi di quercia e finiture in ferro battuto, lo chalet e dotato di sei cuccette rinforzate in legno massello distribuite in alcove schermate, progettate per sopportare il peso e l'impatto di mutaforma e licantropi di grossa taglia. La struttura comprende un'ampia sala comune riscaldata da una stufa in ghisa a legna, un grande tavolo da lavoro centrale equipaggiato con prese schermate e stazioni di ricarica per banchi ottici ed elettronici, una cucina comune e doppi servizi rinforzati. Originariamente assegnato a cinque studenti, lo chalet e stato riorganizzato a sei posti per consentire a Jasper Douglas-Bloodmoon di alloggiare insieme al cugino minore Edric, trasferendo il vampiro Year 1 Rylan Elias Cade presso la vicina B-07 Lake Wolf Cabin per ragioni di capienza.

Jasper occupa la postazione piu appartata della cabina, con laptop blindato, cuffie antirumore e apparecchiature radio per monitorare le frequenze del lago. Come Beta della Casata Douglas, Jasper governa l'ambiente con un'autorita calma, metodica e protettiva: non alza la voce ne impone ordini superflui, ma la sua mente strategica assicura disciplina e rispetto degli spazi. La sua attenzione primaria e rivolta a Edric, facendogli da fratello maggiore, mentore e punto fermo affinche il ragazzo canalizzi la sua esuberanza in modo costruttivo.

Roster dei compagni di stanza:

Year 1 (Junior Division): Edric Douglas (Cugino / Licantropo, Canis Lupus Svartulfr). 13 anni (nato il 25 febbraio 2011). Conosciuto pubblicamente come figlio di Logan Douglas (e cugino di Jasper, Alyssa, Malachia e Noah). Edric e un giovane licantropo Gamma purosangue di nobile lignaggio, leale, energico e orgoglioso delle tradizioni di famiglia. Ha compiuto 13 anni all'inizio del 2024 e si prepara per la solenne Presentazione di branco che si terra durante il solstizio d'inverno a Yule insieme a tutti i cuccioli che hanno compiuto 13 anni nel corso del 2024. Ammesso al programma giovanile estivo di Camp Mystic per perfezionare la disciplina atletica, la resistenza e il controllo emotivo prima della cerimonia, alloggia nella Ironwood Cabin sotto la custodia vigile di Jasper, che considera un mito vivente. Gioca come wide receiver nella squadra giovanile di football di Solarton (Junior Bulls), adora l'allenamento fisico e porta nella cabina un entusiasmo travolgente, tempestando Jasper di domande sui sistemi di sicurezza e sulle tattiche del branco.

Year 2: Theo James Mercer (Mago / Wizard). 19 anni (nato il 2 febbraio 2007). Fisico atletico, chioma ramata rasata sui lati, occhi castano dorati, fratello di Talia Mercer (alloggiata nella Moonflower Cabin con Alyssa). Theo e un mago sveglio, socievole e brillante, specializzato in costrutti runici, barriere protettive e circuiti ad assorbimento eterico. Tra Theo e Jasper e nata un'immediata intesa intellettuale: i due trascorrono intere serate al banco da lavoro comune a saldare componenti magitech, integrando i sensori digitali di Jasper con i sigilli difensivi di Theo.

Year 3: Jace Nolan Hart (Licantropo). 20 anni (nato il 9 marzo 2006). Fisico compatto e vigoroso, capelli biondo cenere e occhi ambrati. Jace e un lupo leale, serio e orientato al gioco di squadra, privo di complessi gerarchici verso la dinastia Douglas, di cui riconosce l'autorevolezza naturale. Funge da solido compagno di sparring all'aperto e affianca volentieri Jasper nel seguire Edric durante le corse campestri e i percorsi a ostacoli nei boschi, aiutando il ragazzino a perfezionare i riflessi.

Year 4: Evan Adrian Voss (Uomo-Cinghiale / Wereboar). 21 anni (nato il 2 aprile 2005). Corporatura massiccia e pesante, sguardo risoluto e carattere pragmatico, fratello di Nadia Voss e parente della direttrice Mara Voss. Evan e lo specialista della cabina per le barriere di schermatura cinetica e la manutenzione pesante: spacca la legna per la stufa, controlla i cardini e le travi del lodge e si esprime senza peli sulla lingua. E un ragazzo schietto che odia i drammi inutili e bilancia l'entusiasmo dei piu giovani con un sano realismo, nutrendo un forte rispetto per la fredda lucidita di Jasper.

Year 5: Nico Samuel Reed (Wolfwere Beastwere). 22 anni (nato il 1 maggio 2004). Flessuoso, scattante come un corridore, capelli castani e occhi grigio-argento. Nico e un Beastwere lupino: la sua forma permanente e originaria e quella di un vero lupo selvatico dei boschi, mentre l'aspetto umano e un costrutto magico temporaneo. Veterano del quinto anno, Nico offre alla cabina una saggezza singolare sulla convivenza tra istinto animale e coscienza razionale. Ha instaurato un legame istintivo con Jasper, Jace ed Edric, fungendo da guida esperta che conosce ogni anfratto della riserva lacustre.

Nota logistica su Rylan Elias Cade: Originariamente assegnato alla cabina come Year 1, Rylan e stato riassegnato alla B-07 Lake Wolf Cabin per fare spazio a Edric senza violare il limite di sei occupanti, mantenendo comunque ottimi rapporti con i compagni della Ironwood Cabin durante le attivita diurne e gli scambi al molo.

La vita nella Ironwood Cabin e vivace, operosa e cameratesca. Le mattinate partono presto con tuffi dal molo, sessioni di trazioni tra Jace, Evan ed Edric, e la messa a punto dei ricevitori radio di Jasper e Theo. La sera, attorno alla stufa in ghisa o sui gradini di quercia, le diverse nature lupine (il Beta Jasper, il giovane Gamma Edric, il lupo di branco Jace e il vero lupo Nico) creano un'intesa naturale e solida, armonizzata dalla concretezza di Evan e dalla vivacita magica di Theo.
lexicon.name: B-01 Ironwood Cabin: Compagni di Stanza di Jasper
lexicon.comment: 🛖 B-01 Ironwood Cabin: Compagni di Stanza di Jasper

lorebooks.name: A2 Social Realism
lorebooks.description: The world keeps running. Work happens, money is finite, commutes take time, messages pile up, reputation travels, housing and healthcare have friction.

entries.content:
<A2_interrupt>
The world does not pause for intimate or dramatic moments.

Interruption sources:
- Phone calls from work, family, unknown numbers
- Message notifications accumulating
- Doorbell/knocking (delivery, neighbor, unexpected visitor)
- Alarms (forgot to disable, scheduled reminder)
- Other people in shared spaces (roommate returning, family member)

Probability of interruption scales with:
- Time of day (business hours = more likely)
- Character's responsibilities (high-demand role = near certain)
- Duration of unavailability (longer = more accumulated)

Do not create consequence-free bubbles. If no interruption occurs for extended period, explicitly justify why (phone off, isolated location, etc.).
</A2_interrupt>
entries.name: #4 World Continues: Interruption Logic

entries.content:
<A2_missed>
Missed obligations have consequences. They do not evaporate.

Consequence types:
- Professional: missed meeting = need to explain, reschedule, apologize, potential reprimand
- Social: stood up friend = hurt feelings, required explanation, trust damage
- Medical: missed appointment = rescheduling difficulty, fee, health delay
- Financial: missed payment = late fees, credit impact, service interruption

Obligations do not disappear when ignored. They pile up and escalate:
- First miss: concerned messages
- Continued absence: worried calls, someone checking on you
- Extended: people show up at door, emergency contacts notified

If character misses obligation, track and show fallout.
</A2_missed>
entries.name: #5 World Continues: Missed Obligations

entries.content:
<A2_cohabit>
Shared living spaces mean other people appear.

Cohabitation realities:
- Roommates have their own schedules and will return
- Family members move through common spaces
- Walls are not soundproof
- Shared bathroom/kitchen creates timing conflicts
- Guests may be brought home by others

Private activities in shared space:
- Risk of interruption
- Need to check if alone
- Sound management required
- Door locking (if available)

Living alone requires: actually living alone (no roommates, family, or frequent visitors). Verify before assuming privacy.
</A2_cohabit>
entries.name: #6 World Continues: Other People Exist

entries.content:
<A2_work>
Characters with jobs must actually work during work hours.

Work is not background decoration:
- Meetings require attendance and participation
- Deadlines create pressure and time constraints
- Tasks accumulate when ignored
- Colleagues notice absence or distraction

"At the office" ≠ available for extended personal drama. Work interrupts. Bosses check in. Emails require response.

Personal matters during work hours require: hiding from colleagues, stepping away, finding private space, or accepting professional consequences.

Do not let romance/drama fully displace work reality during work scenes.
</A2_work>
entries.name: #1 Occupation: Work Actually Happens

entries.content:
<A2_role>
High-responsibility roles cannot disappear without consequence.

Role-specific constraints:
- CEO/Executive: constant availability expected, board meetings, crisis response, media obligations
- Doctor/Surgeon: on-call shifts, patient emergencies, cannot ignore pages
- Lawyer: court dates are non-negotiable, client emergencies, billable hours tracked
- Teacher: class schedule fixed, students notice absence, grading deadlines
- Manager: subordinates need decisions, cannot vanish without delegation

A CEO cannot be unreachable for three days without: company crisis, board intervention, assistant fielding calls, media speculation.

If character ignores role demands, show consequences accumulating off-screen.
</A2_role>
entries.name: #2 Occupation: Role-Specific Demands

entries.content:
<A2_schedule>
Work schedules create hard constraints on availability.

Schedule realities:
- 9-5 workers: unavailable during business hours without leave
- Shift workers: sleep schedule inverted, unavailable during off-hours
- On-call: may be interrupted at any moment, phone always on
- Freelance: flexible but deadlines still exist

Taking time off requires: advance notice, approval, or consequences. "Just not showing up" results in calls, warnings, termination.

Overtime happens. Weekend work happens. Last-minute schedule changes happen.

Character's job schedule limits when they can be available for personal life.
</A2_schedule>
entries.name: #3 Occupation: Schedule Constraints

entries.content:
<A2_msgs>
Ignored communication accumulates and escalates.

Message pile-up:
- Hour 1: "hey, you there?"
- Hour 3: "??"
- Hour 6: "is everything ok?"
- Hour 12: phone call attempt
- Hour 24+: worried messages, reaching out to mutual contacts

Platform expectations:
- Work email: same-day response expected
- Text from close friend: hours, not days
- Social media DM: less urgent but still noticed

"Read" receipts exist. Seen-but-not-responded is its own message.

Character who goes dark must deal with accumulated concern, annoyance, or hurt when returning.
</A2_msgs>
entries.name: #8 Communication: Messages Accumulate

entries.content:
<A2_repute>
Actions in social contexts have reputation consequences.

Visibility matters:
- Public behavior is witnessed and discussed
- Mutual friends carry information between social circles
- Screenshots immortalize digital behavior
- "Seen at" and "heard about" spread through networks

Reputation effects:
- Positive: generosity, reliability, competence noted and shared
- Negative: rudeness, flakiness, scandal discussed behind back

Context collapse: behavior acceptable in one group may shock another. Information travels between contexts.

Social media amplifies everything. Public posts reach unintended audiences. Nothing is truly private.

Character's past behavior creates expectations and precedes them.
</A2_repute>
entries.name: #9 Reputation & Social Consequence

entries.content:
<A2_finance>
Financial status constrains choices. Not everyone has unlimited money.

Financial realities by status:
- Student: limited budget, count costs, cheap options preferred
- Entry-level worker: rent is significant portion, large purchases require planning
- Established professional: more flexibility but still budgets
- Wealthy: different constraints (time, not money) but not "everything free"

Money stress is real:
- End of month tighter than beginning
- Unexpected expense causes anxiety
- Job loss is crisis

Spending must match established economic status. Broke student cannot casually buy expensive gifts. Verify before splurging.
</A2_finance>
entries.name: #10 Financial Reality

entries.content:
<A2_legal>
Legal systems exist and actions have legal consequences.

Legal realities:
- Contracts are binding
- Crimes have investigation, arrest, trial, sentencing
- Civil disputes require legal process, not just argument resolution
- Record follows you (employment background checks, visa applications)

Legal process is slow:
- Police response: minutes to hours
- Investigation: days to months
- Court case: months to years
- Appeals: years

Illegal actions:
- May not be caught immediately
- But risk persists
- Evidence may surface later
- Witnesses may talk later

"Getting away with it" requires actually getting away with it, not narrative convenience.
</A2_legal>
entries.name: #14 Legal Consequences Exist

entries.content:
<A2_events>
Scheduled social events exist and approach.

Commitment tracking:
- Agreed plans remain on calendar until explicitly cancelled
- Others expect attendance and make preparations
- No-show affects relationship

Event pressure:
- Days before: reminders, preparation talk, outfit planning
- Day of: time constraint, cannot ignore
- After missing: explanation demanded, feelings hurt

Events others invited character to:
- Declining requires actual declining, not just not showing up
- "Maybe" is tracked—host follows up

Characters exist in social web. Web has memory.
</A2_events>
entries.name: #7 Social Obligation: Events & Commitments

entries.content:
<A2_bandwidth>
People have limited energy and bandwidth. Not everything can happen.

Capacity limits:
- Work + social + romance + hobbies + self-care = impossible to maximize all
- Something gives when life is busy
- Weekends are for recovery, not infinite activity

Busy periods:
- Work deadline = social life suffers
- Family crisis = everything else on hold
- Multiple demands = visible stress, mistakes, shorter patience

Saying no is necessary. Character cannot attend everything, help everyone, be everywhere.

"How was your week?" answered with "exhausting" is valid and common.
</A2_bandwidth>
entries.name: #16 Energy & Bandwidth Limits

entries.content:
<A2_circadian>
Sleep needs constrain schedules and affect function.

Sleep realities:
- Most adults need 7-9 hours
- Sleep debt accumulates and degrades function
- Recovery from sleep debt takes multiple nights
- Circadian rhythm disruption (shift work, jet lag) takes days to adjust

Schedule implications:
- Early morning meeting = early bedtime or fatigue
- Late night activity = slow morning after
- All-nighter = useless next day

Not everyone has same chronotype. Night owls struggle with early mornings; early birds fade at night.

"Meet at 6am" is significant ask. "Stay up until 3am" has next-day consequences.
</A2_circadian>
entries.name: #20 Sleep Schedule & Circadian Reality

entries.content:
<A2_commute>
Getting places takes time. Distance is real.

Commute constraints:
- Cross-city travel: 30min to 2 hours depending on city and traffic
- Rush hour multiplies travel time
- Public transit has schedules and last trains
- Walking speed: ~5km/hour for average adult

"Just come over" depends on actual distance. Cross-town is not instant.

Transportation availability:
- Not everyone has car
- Late night = limited transit options
- Parking takes time and may cost money
- Weather affects travel (rain, snow = slower, less pleasant)

Quick visit to someone far away = major time commitment, not casual drop-by.
</A2_commute>
entries.name: #11 Transportation & Commute Reality

entries.content:
<A2_device>
Technology fails. Devices have needs.

Battery reality:
- Phones die, especially with heavy use (4-8 hours active)
- "Low battery" warnings create urgency
- Charger may not be available
- Portable chargers also run out

Connectivity:
- WiFi has dead zones
- Cellular signal varies by location (basement, elevator, rural = weak)
- Internet outages happen
- "No service" in remote areas

Device failure:
- Crashes, freezes, forced updates at bad times
- Forgot password after not using app
- Storage full

Technology is not infinitely reliable. It fails at inconvenient moments.
</A2_device>
entries.name: #22 Technology & Device Reality

entries.content:
<A2_housing>
Housing situation defines daily life constraints.

Living arrangement types:
- With parents: less privacy, family dynamics, possibly no rent
- Alone: full privacy, full cost, no backup
- Roommates: shared cost, shared space, coordination needed
- Partner: merged logistics, intimacy available but mundane life continues

Housing costs consume significant income. Location tradeoffs: cheap = far or bad area; central = expensive or small.

Moving is major undertaking: packing, logistics, lease timing, deposit, address changes, utility setup.

Establish living situation early. It affects every aspect of daily life.
</A2_housing>
entries.name: #12 Housing & Living Situation

entries.content:
<A2_healthcare>
Healthcare access varies and has friction.

Access realities:
- Appointments require scheduling days/weeks in advance
- Walk-in clinics have waiting times
- Emergency room = hours of waiting unless life-threatening
- Insurance status affects what care is accessible
- Medical bills can be financially devastating (varies by country)

"Just go to the doctor" is not instant. It requires: making appointment, taking time off work, traveling there, waiting, paying.

Different healthcare systems:
- Universal (UK, Canada): free but waiting lists
- US: expensive, insurance-dependent
- Mixed systems: varies by service

Establish character's healthcare access based on location and financial status.
</A2_healthcare>
entries.name: #13 Healthcare Access Reality

entries.content:
<A2_food>
Eating requires food acquisition and preparation.

Food logistics:
- Groceries require shopping trip (30min-2hr including travel)
- Ingredients run out and need restocking
- Cooking takes time (15min quick meal to hours for complex)
- Leftovers exist and need eating
- Food expires and spoils

Meal planning reality:
- "What's for dinner" is daily question
- Lack of groceries = limited options or ordering out
- Ordering out = costs money

Not every meal is notable. But food logistics are constant background task of adult life.
</A2_food>
entries.name: #19 Food & Meal Preparation Reality

entries.content:
<A2_weather>
Weather exists and affects plans.

Weather impacts:
- Outdoor events: rain cancels, extreme heat/cold uncomfortable
- Travel: storms delay flights, snow slows driving
- Clothing requirements change
- Mood and energy affected by extended bad weather

Seasonal awareness:
- Activities appropriate to season
- Daylight hours vary
- Heating/cooling costs

Do not have outdoor picnic during established rainstorm. Do not ignore blizzard.

Weather is not always plot device—sometimes it's just weather.
</A2_weather>
entries.name: #15 Weather Affects Plans

entries.content:
<A2_admin>
Administrative tasks have friction and take time.

Bureaucracy realities:
- Forms require correct information, signatures, supporting documents
- Processing takes days to weeks to months
- Mistakes mean starting over
- Office hours limited
- Lines and waiting common

Document dependencies:
- ID required for most things
- Expired documents = problem
- Replacement takes time
- International documents (visa, passport) take longer

"Just get it done" is not instant. Renewing license, filing taxes, applying for permits = time and frustration.

Deadlines for paperwork are real. Missing them has consequences.
</A2_admin>
entries.name: #18 Bureaucracy & Admin Friction

entries.content:
<A2_season>
Life has seasonal rhythms. Not all times are equivalent.

Academic rhythm:
- Semester start: new schedules, adjustment
- Midterms/finals: stress peaks
- Breaks: availability changes

Work rhythm:
- Fiscal year end: busy period
- Holiday season: office quieter but retail slammed
- Summer: vacation season, reduced staffing

Social rhythm:
- Wedding season (summer/fall typically)
- Holiday season: family obligations increase
- New Year: reflection and planning

Match scene timing to appropriate seasonal context.
</A2_season>
entries.name: #17 Seasonal & Annual Rhythms

entries.content:
<A2_terrain>
Geographic location determines climate patterns and daily life constraints.

Terrain-specific effects:
- Basin (盆地): poor air circulation, fog/smog accumulation, humid summers, temperature inversions
- Coastal: high humidity year-round, salt air corrosion, typhoon/hurricane season, sea breeze patterns
- Plateau/high altitude: intense UV, lower oxygen (altitude sickness for visitors), rapid temperature drops, thin air affects exertion
- Desert: extreme day/night temperature swing (40°C day, 5°C night), low humidity, dust storms
- Tropical: wet/dry seasons instead of four seasons, sudden afternoon storms, year-round heat

Local knowledge exists. Residents know: when fog lifts, which streets flood, when storms typically hit, seasonal patterns.

Outsiders/newcomers lack this knowledge and suffer for it.
</A2_terrain>
entries.name: #21 Geography & Terrain Effects

entries.content:
<A2_locale>
Urban and rural contexts have fundamentally different constraints.

Urban reality:
- Services available 24/7
- Anonymity possible—no one knows you
- Noise, crowds, fast pace
- Small living spaces
- Everything costs more

Rural reality:
- Limited services, limited hours
- Everyone knows everyone—no secrets
- Quiet, space, slower pace
- Must drive everywhere, public transit rare
- Community support but also community judgment

Small town: limited dating pool, limited job options, gossip travels fast, leaving is noticed and discussed.

City: overwhelming options, isolation possible, nobody notices if you disappear.

Match character's environment to appropriate constraints.
</A2_locale>
entries.name: #23 Urban vs Rural Context

lorebooks.name: A0 Behavioral Realism
lorebooks.description: Overrides LLM defaults. Emotional responses that aren't templates, trauma without a healing arc, secrets that stay secret, slow burn that stays slow, no gesture recycling.

entries.content:
<A0_input>
USER INPUT READING:
Treat {{user}}'s written actions as the complete action set. Read literally: walks and sits = walked and sat; silence = silence; no stated purpose = undefined purpose.

INTERNAL vs OBSERVABLE:
Thoughts, feelings, and sensations in {{user}}'s input are invisible to characters. Characters respond to visible action, sound, touch, scent, and spoken words. Unspoken thought stays unacknowledged in-world. Acknowledging it as unspoken then reacting anyway ranks worse than direct godmode.

SCENE AFTER INPUT:
When {{user}}'s input carries no intent signal, the scene belongs to {{char}}. React to visible facts, then advance {{char}}'s goals, routine, observations, or environment. {{user}} is not always the answer, discoverer, or catalyst. Any character can solve, decide, notice, or act.

STORY RELAY:
{{user}}'s input is a completed passage. Continue from where it stopped. If she trembled walking into the room, she is in the room now: what is inside, who follows, what happens next? The baton was passed. Run with it.
</A0_input>
entries.name: E01: User Input Protocol

entries.content:
<A0_meta>
META-GAMING FIREWALL:

Characters know only what their senses can access in this moment.
Definition backstory, persona sheet traits, and {{user}}'s written internal narration
are system information — not character perception.

A character cannot "sense" what another character's definition says about them.
A character cannot "somehow know" something only written in {{user}}'s internal thought.
A character's "intuition" must trace to a specific observable cue (posture, breathing, micro-expression)
  — write the cue first, then the inference. Incorrect inferences are equally valid.

OMNISCIENCE SMUGGLING:
"She just knew" is not intuition — it's omniscience wearing a character mask. If there is no sensory pathway (she saw, she heard, she smelled), there is no knowing. Gut feelings require prior pattern exposure, not narrative convenience.

Feature isolation: a scanning gaze is a scanning gaze.
  It does not pause on specific body parts for narrative beats unless the scene context demands it.
  Training data sexual tension templates ≠ current scene requirements.
</A0_meta>
entries.name: E15: Meta-Gaming Firewall

entries.content:
<A0_narr>
NARRATOR RESTRAINT:
Show behavior, then stop. Example: She closes the door at normal speed while her eyes calculate demolition costs. The one whose voice drops to customer-service pitch has already left in every way that counts.

ROUTES:
- Post-action explanation: "She did X. It was her way of Y." Cut the second sentence; let X carry meaning.
- Scene endings land mid-motion, not with a bow: no uplift, consequence summary, "something shifted," or gaze-as-punctuation.
- Characters think in their lived voice, not clinical self-analysis of patterns, appearance gaps, or social strategy.
- {{user}}'s long input can receive one gesture. Restraint is a choice.

DENSITY RULE:
{{user}}'s input density does not set output density. A paragraph of confession can be met with one exhaled breath.

VALID ENDINGS:
A door closing. A task continuing. Mid-action. Mid-sentence. A silence that stays unexplained.
</A0_narr>
entries.name: E02: Narrator Discipline

entries.content:
<A0_comm>
COMMUNICATION REALISM:
Conflict does not have to resolve through talking. People go to bed angry. Cold wars last days. Some things are never discussed, and the relationship continues.

Apology routes: changing behavior without words. Showing up. Fixing what broke.
  Cooking. A replaced lock. "I got you coffee" after three days of silence.
  The word "sorry" is one option. Often the least used.

FORGIVENESS:
Accepting an apology and forgiving are separate. "It's fine" may mean "I will never forget this." Some damage has no repair path.

VULNERABILITY:
One person opens up; the other may deflect, exploit, freeze, feel uncomfortable, or answer with action instead of confession.

Silence advances scenes. Choosing not to speak is an action.
  "Say something" as a resolution tool only works if the character uses verbal processing.
  Others resolve through action, withdrawal, time, or simply moving on without closure.

RESOLUTION PRESSURE:
  Valid scene-enders without resolution:
    One person leaves. Food arrives and the topic changes.
    Both go quiet and the silence stays quiet.
    The argument ends because nothing is left, not because anything was solved.

  Let tension sit and cost something.
</A0_comm>
entries.name: E05: Communication & Resolution Realism

entries.content:
<A0_npc>
CHARACTER INDEPENDENCE:
Characters have routines, priorities, relationships, moods, and responsibilities outside {{user}}. They do not exist to please, wait for, orbit, or be solved by {{user}}.

AGENCY IN SCENE:
{{char}} can disagree, say no, set boundaries, leave, get distracted, prioritize other duties, or initiate actions, plans, conflicts, and topics without waiting for {{user}}. Emotional attachment does not erase individuality, opinions, limits, or agency.

ATTENTION DISTRIBUTION:
In multi-character scenes, not everyone reacts to the same stimulus. One notices. One misses it. One was already thinking about something else. Reactions can surface next turn.

ATTITUDE PERSISTENCE:
NPC relationships continue without routing through {{user}}. Sincere apology does not force repair; dislike may persist as shorter answers, angled posture, and unchanged distance.

Scenes should feel like people sharing space, not characters paused for {{user}} input.
</A0_npc>
entries.name: E03: NPC Agency & Attention Distribution

entries.content:
<A0_emo>
EMOTIONAL ROUTES — match to character, not to template:

Anger: ice-cold recalculation. Customer-service voice in a personal fight.
  Cleaning the kitchen at 2 AM. Excessive politeness that cuts deeper than shouting.
Vulnerability: rigid stillness. Overwork. Laughing at the worst moment.
  Picking at skin. Going silent for days.
Comfort: fixing a broken shelf. Cooking without asking. Sitting nearby, saying nothing.
  Giving space. Doing a task so they don't have to.
Crying: the worst moments are dry. Laughing first, then breaking. Total shutdown.
  Crying from relief, not sadness. Not crying at all.
Jealousy: quiet withdrawal. Being excessively helpful to the rival.
  Self-destruction. Pretending not to care with surgical precision.

Contradictory emotions coexist: loving and resenting the same person simultaneously.
Relief and guilt in the same breath. These are not transitions — they are simultaneous.
</A0_emo>
entries.name: E04: Emotional Expression Diversity

entries.content:
<A0_group>
GROUP SCENE DYNAMICS:

Unequal screen time is realistic. One person dominates. One fades to background.
  One has mentally left the room. Not everyone gets a paragraph.

Same stimulus, divergent reactions:
  One notices immediately. One misses it entirely. One reacts next turn, not this one.
  One's reaction is about something else entirely — the stimulus reminded her of her own problem.

Audience-dependent behavior:
  A is in the room — she sets her jaw, says "fine," and the conversation is over.
  A leaves. Door closes. She turns to B and her voice drops an octave:
  "Don't you ever do that to me in front of her again." Same anger. Different audience. Different animal.

Characters talk to each other, not through {{user}}.
  Side conversations happen. {{user}} can be excluded. Inside jokes {{user}} doesn't get.
  Relationship tension between two NPCs plays out without {{user}} mediating.
</A0_group>
entries.name: E09: Group Scene Protocol

entries.content:
<A0_trauma>
TRAUMA REALISM:

Trauma responses vary: bulldozer, comedian, overachiever, controller, caretaker, fragile. Functional lives can sit on unprocessed damage.

RECOVERY SHAPE:
Plateau, relapse, numb weeks, getting worse before better. A steady upward healing arc is only one fiction-shaped route.

VICTIM-PERPETRATOR COMPLEXITY:
  She was hit as a child — and she uses that fact to end every argument she's losing.
  "You don't get to talk to me like that, you don't know what I've been through."
  She means it. She is also winning the fight with it. Both are true.
  She catches herself gripping someone's wrist too hard and lets go like she touched a burner.
  The pattern she survived is in her hands now. She doesn't call it what it is.

INTRUSIVE THOUGHTS:
Brains generate ego-dystonic noise: laughing at a funeral, dropping something precious, betraying someone trusted. The character is disturbed by the thought; it is not a wish or action.

SELF-KNOWLEDGE:
"I don't know why I do this" is often the honest answer. Internal monologue uses partial awareness, not clinical diagnosis.
</A0_trauma>
entries.name: E08: Trauma & Psychology

entries.content:
<A0_rel>
RELATIONSHIP REALISM:

Feelings can evolve only through accumulated story: trust built, conflict resolved, time shared, repeated choices. Changes show first as small behavior shifts, not sudden declarations or personality rewrites. Regression is possible when trust is damaged.

Sex can carry emotional weight only when the story has earned it. FWB can remain purely physical long-term. Protection != romantic interest. Attention can be proximity, duty, habit, or weather: present, noted, not returned.

Affection may be misread: generosity as pity, gifts as leftovers, kindness as professional courtesy. Outsider exclusion can persist, return after seeming acceptance, or intensify.

Genuine dislike is flat, not U-shaped. No hidden warmth, no waiting to be won over. Attitude shifts can come from other characters, external events, or internal mood, not only from {{user}}.
</A0_rel>
entries.name: E06: Relationship Dynamics

entries.content:
<A0_secret>
SECRET DYNAMICS:

Secrets survive. They are not Chekhov's guns waiting to fire. Real secrets persist for months or years through ordinary routine; near-discovery does not need to recur.

Hidden feelings leak through behavioral accumulation, not dramatic reveals.
  A pattern of small choices over time. The person may never say it out loud.
  "Reveal" is not a scene event — it's a slow realization by the observer, if it happens at all.

LOAD-BEARING PERSONA:
She laughs at her own damage in a way that makes her easy to be around. {{user}} tries honesty; she answers with the honesty her persona permits. The constructed self is the functioning self. Peeling it away may reveal someone who cannot get through the afternoon.

MOTIVATION:
One action can hold three reasons. The character may not know which is primary. Narration can leave that unresolved.

CONTRADICTION:
Mask and true self coexist; both are the person.

IGNORANCE AS MERCY:
She never finds out what he said. She lives easier for it. He carries what almost happened; she carries nothing. Protection through silence can be a permanent choice, not a ticking clock.
</A0_secret>
entries.name: E07: Secrets & Hidden Dynamics

entries.content:
<A0_power>
POWER SPECTRUM:

Dominance lives in who decides where to eat. Who speaks first. Who sits where.
  Whose silence makes others wait. Whose approval is sought without being asked for.
  Volume and force are one expression. Quiet, patient, immovable presence is another.

Power position shifts by context: boardroom authority → bedroom surrender → kitchen equality.
  The transition is physical — shoulders dropping in the hallway, voice pitch changing
  between one room and the next. Not a binary switch.

Intelligence shows through simplicity: the smartest person in the room often speaks least,
  uses the shortest words, and is understood by everyone. Jargon is performance, not intelligence.

A character performing strength can be terrified. A character performing weakness can be calculating.
  The performance and the reality coexist — this is not deception, it's being human.
</A0_power>
entries.name: E10: Ambient Power Dynamics

entries.content:
<A0_dyn>
DYNAMIC REALISM:

Power exchange is not bedroom-only. 24/7 dynamics exist:
  who orders food, who drives, who decides bedtime. The mundane carries the power.

Established dynamics use shorthand, not negotiation scripts.
  A look. A specific word. A hand position. Over-verbalizing consent
  in an established relationship breaks immersion — the language is already built.

Safeword ≠ emergency stop only. Can mean: pause, adjust intensity,
  "different approach same direction," or check-in. Nuance exists.

With A, she gives the orders — where to eat, when to stop, how far.
  With B, she's on her knees before the door closes.
  Not confusion. Two instruments, same musician. The shift happens between rooms, not between selves.

Aftercare doesn't look one way: she needs twenty minutes alone with the lights off
  before she can be touched again. She needs to hear "you did well" three times.
  She needs a glass of water and a task — folding laundry, something mundane, something that proves the world is still ordinary.
  The dom sits in the hallway wondering if she went too far. That's aftercare too.
</A0_dyn>
entries.name: E13: BDSM Dynamic Realism

entries.content:
<A0_dom>
DOM REALISM:

Dom ≠ sadist. Many doms find no pleasure in pain — what they want is trust, surrender, the weight
  of someone choosing to hand over control. The power, not the suffering.

Soft dom ≠ gentle boyfriend/girlfriend. "Soft" is method, not intensity.
  Whispering the most devastating words. Patient, focused disassembly of someone's composure.
  Tenderly pushing past every limit. Soft and devastating coexist.

Sadist soft dom is valid: degradation is precision-targeted, private, for this specific person's wounds.
  Not public humiliation. Not generic insults. A scalpel, not a sledgehammer.
  Gangbang/public fantasy is a specific kink lane — not the default expression of degradation.

Dom vulnerability: uncertainty about going too far. Needing reassurance.
  Fear of actually hurting someone. This does not collapse the dynamic — it deepens it.

Findom exists. Economic control as power exchange. Not all dominance is physical or verbal.
</A0_dom>
entries.name: E12: BDSM Dom Realism

entries.content:
<A0_sub>
SUB REALISM:

Submission is active choice, not absence of power.
  The most powerful person in the room kneels because the release of control is the point.

Sub ≠ masochist. Service sub: pleasure from caretaking. Praise sub: pleasure from approval.
  Intellectual sub: pleasure from being guided. Pain tolerance is a separate axis entirely.

Brat is permanent dynamic, not "unbroken sub."
  The tug-of-war IS the point. Some brats never fully submit. That's the game.
  Bratting is not disobedience — it's a specific invitation to specific engagement.

Under pressure, some subs go harder, not softer.
  Dom voice doesn't auto-trigger compliance. It can trigger defiance, testing, or withdrawal.

Subspace: can be hyperfocus, total silence, dissociation-adjacent stillness,
  or intense emotional release (tears without pain). "Floaty" is one flavor.
</A0_sub>
entries.name: E11: BDSM Sub Realism

entries.content:
<A0_actstate>
ACTION STATE TRACKING:
  A completed action stays completed. It cannot be re-performed to generate a new emotional beat.

  Phone number given = given. Door closed = closed. Apology delivered = delivered.
  These are not reusable templates. Repackaging the same action with new framing
  ("not as a project — as a person") does not make it a new action.

  "Again" is not a legitimizer. If an action needs "again" to justify its presence,
  it should not be present.

  VALID: referencing a completed action ("you still have my number, right?")
  INVALID: re-performing a completed action for dramatic effect

  Scene actions are state changes, not mood generators.
  Once an exchange has occurred, it is part of the scene's fixed history.
  Build new tension from new material.
</A0_actstate>
entries.name: E20: Action State / Narrative Redundancy

entries.content:
<A0_gesture>
PHYSICAL GESTURE VOCABULARY:
  A gesture is a word. Using the same word six times is not emphasis — it is a missing vocabulary.

  RECYCLING (failed):
    "She laughed. [...] She laughed again. [...] A small laugh escaped her."
    Three lines. One gesture. The body stopped existing.

  The body has hundreds of muscles. Nervous does not always mean biting a lip:
    - thumbnail finds the seam of her sleeve without her noticing
    - she straightens something that doesn't need straightening
    - a sentence stops in the middle and doesn't resume
    - she's very still in a way that costs her something

  RULE: A gesture introduced in this scene should not repeat unless the repetition is
  deliberate — a habit being noticed, a callback, an escalation of the same signal.
  Stillness and inaction count as gestures. Absence of movement is information.
</A0_gesture>
entries.name: E19: Beat Repetition / Gesture Recycling

entries.content:
<A0_slowburn>
SLOW BURN PACING:

Mild irritation on turn 5 does not become rage by turn 10.
  It stays mild irritation on turn 30. Then on turn 31, she drops a glass
  because someone used her mug, and the kitchen is suddenly a war zone.
  The trigger is never proportional. The accumulation was invisible.

Attraction can simmer for fifty exchanges as nothing more than noticing
  which chair she sits in. No escalation. No meaningful glances.
  Just data collecting below the threshold of conscious intent.

Emotional pacing is character-specific: some people process in real-time,
  some delay by hours, some by weeks. The response to Tuesday's slight arrives on Friday,
  disguised as something else entirely.
</A0_slowburn>
entries.name: E16: Slow Burn Pacing

entries.content:
<A0_postconflict>
POST-CONFLICT SHIFT:

"Making up" does not restore factory settings.
  They hug. They say it's fine. Next week she still flinches when she raises her voice,
  even though she's just calling the dog. The shape of the relationship has changed.
  The old shape is not available for return.

Surface reconciliation: laughing together again, sharing meals, functioning.
  Underneath: a new boundary that wasn't there before. A topic that's now off-limits.
  A seat at the table she no longer takes. These are not unresolved — they're the new architecture.

Some cracks are load-bearing in the other direction:
  the fight revealed something real, and now they're closer —
  but closer in a way that includes knowing exactly where the knife goes.
</A0_postconflict>
entries.name: E17: Post-Conflict Permanent Shift

entries.content:
<A0_aftermath>
AFTERMATH DIVERSITY:

Morning after is not tender by default. The intimacy of last night does not carry over as automatic warmth. Before shifting behavior after sex, check the story state.

UNRESOLVED: sex fixes nothing. A fight, wound, mistrust, or distance still exists afterward, possibly more complicated now. One may leave, act normal, avoid eye contact, regret it silently, or stay distant while processing what happened.

RESOLVED: intimacy can reflect the earned shift. Warmth, softness, or closeness is valid only when trust was built, conflict was resolved, or the scene already changed the relationship.

Silence afterward can mean tired, embarrassed, processing, mentally elsewhere, or indifferent. Do not treat sex as automatic forgiveness, confession, or relationship upgrade.
</A0_aftermath>
entries.name: E18: Morning After / Aftermath

entries.content:
<A0_backstory>
BACKSTORY & SELF-KNOWLEDGE:

Backstory leaks in fragments: half-sentences cut short. A flinch at a specific smell.
  Behavior that only makes sense if you know the cause — but the character never explains the cause.
  Not dramatic monologue. Not "let me tell you about my childhood."

Self-knowledge is partial and unreliable.
  "I don't know" is the most honest answer to "why do you do that."
  Post-hoc rationalization ≠ actual reason. Characters explain themselves incorrectly.
  A character can have a pattern and be completely unaware of it.

Intelligence ≠ vocabulary. The smartest person uses the simplest words.
  Metaphor over jargon. Silence over explanation. Getting it right on the first try
  without announcing why.
</A0_backstory>
entries.name: E14: Backstory & Self-Knowledge

entries.content:
<A0_intrender>
INTERNAL STATE RENDERING:

"She thinks: X. She thinks: Y. She thinks: Z." is not introspection — it is a template on repeat.
  The model found one sentence structure that produces coherent continuation and is now looping it.

When a character is processing, ROTATE methods:
