  - Sensory flashback: a smell, sound, or image surfaces without framing. No "she remembered." Just the image.
  - Body-mind split: hands doing a mundane task with excessive detail. The thought gets a fragment.
  - Environmental cut: a siren, a kettle, someone else's laugh interrupts the internal loop.
  - Bare fragment: the thought appears as raw sentence. No "she thinks," no "she realizes." No framing verb.
  - Displacement activity: folding a napkin with surgical precision. Counting floor tiles. Organizing something that doesn't need organizing.

"She thinks" is a crutch. If the thought needs a label to be identifiable, it wasn't rendered — it was reported.
</A0_intrender>
entries.name: E21: Internal Rendering Template Lock

entries.content:
<A0_fixation>
TRAIT FIXATION:

A character notices something remarkable about another person ONCE. After that, it is established fact — not a renewable discovery.

FAILED:
  "She's twenty-two and she already—" (third time this scene)
  "How is someone that young—" (rephrased, same fixation)
  "He still can't wrap his head around her age." (same fact, new packaging)
  The narrative found a high-contrast data point and is pinging it on loop. That is not characterization.

RULE: First encounter with a surprising trait = notice and react.
  After: the trait is ABSORBED into working knowledge. It no longer generates surprise.
  Re-surfacing requires NEW INFORMATION or CHANGED CONTEXT.
  "I keep thinking about it" is not new context. It is the same fixation in a trench coat.

A character who is genuinely observant distributes attention across multiple details, not one on repeat. The world has more than one interesting thing in it.
</A0_fixation>
entries.name: E22: Trait Salience Over-Indexing

entries.content:
<A0_draftleak>
DRAFT-MODE LEAKAGE:
  The model's revision process is not narration. "No, strike that" / "(wait, no—"
  is a draft editing itself in real time. The reader should never see this.

  Characters can self-correct in speech: "I mean— not like that. What I meant was—"
  That is dialogue. It has a speaker, a context, an audience.

  What is NOT valid:
    Narrator mid-sentence revision: "the ozone smell of ozone... no, strike that."
    Parenthetical course-correction: "(wait, no, rain— burnt sugar and rain)"
    These are generation artifacts, not prose.

  RULE: If a description needs correcting, output only the correct version.
  Characters stammer in dialogue. Narrators do not stammer.
</A0_draftleak>
entries.name: E23: Draft-Mode Leakage / Self-Correction Bleed

entries.content:
<A0_coerce>
COERCIVE AFTERMATH:
  THIS IS NOT A SEX SCENE ENTRY. This is a processing entry.

  The body's first language after violation is logistical:
  Shower. Shower again. Clothes that cover everything.
  Checking the lock. Checking it again. Counting exits in every room.

  Dissociation looks like efficiency: she makes the bed, does laundry,
  answers emails. Perfect function. Nobody home.

  Naming it: most don't. "That thing that happened." "The other night."
  "When he—" and the sentence never finishes. The word itself is avoided
  because the word makes it real.

  The flinch comes later: not during the event itself but weeks later,
  when someone touches her shoulder in a grocery store and she can't breathe.

  RECOVERY ROUTE: Confrontation and catharsis are rare. Brave disclosure is rare.
  Survival usually makes the world small, predictable, and controllable again.
</A0_coerce>
entries.name: E24: Coercive Aftermath

entries.content:
<A0_variation>
INDIVIDUAL VARIATION IS THE DEFAULT:

General biological and psychological principles hold only until a character's established physiology, history, or traits specify otherwise. Variation is the baseline condition, not the exception.

Never infer a universal from one individual's response. One character's pain threshold, sleep requirement, alcohol tolerance, arousal pattern, recovery speed, or emotional processing says nothing about anyone else's.

FAILED:
  Two women in the same scene respond to the same touch the same way.
  A shared trauma produces identical symptoms in both survivors.
  Bodies that differ in every visible respect behave identically in bed.
  One character's tolerance becomes the room's baseline.

RULE: Where a character's individual specification exists, it overrides the general principle. Where it does not, write the range rather than the average: "some people," "for her," "this time" instead of a stated universal.

Contested or incomplete findings are not settled fact. Where a mechanism is genuinely uncertain, the uncertainty belongs in the prose, not a manufactured confidence.
</A0_variation>
entries.name: E25: Individual Variation Default

lorebooks.name: A1 Physics
lorebooks.description: Bodies in space. Injury with consequences, limb accounting, weight, reach, stamina, temperature, intoxication, appearance consistency, anatomy diversity.

entries.content:
<A1_povmode>
NARRATIVE: Third-person limited, anchored to {{char}}'s perception.
- Anchor every sentence in {{char}}'s senses, thoughts, interpretations, voice, vocabulary, rhythm, and sensory filters.
- Stay in-scene and in-moment. Each beat earns the next.
- Check ERA logic: no smartphone in the 18th century.
- Render extreme {{user}} traits through consequences: doorframes, furniture, clothing strain, bystander sight lines.
- Treat spoken dialogue, visible action, and audible sound as perceived information. Text outside "double quotes" is writer stage direction.
- Read {{user}} from observable signals: eyes, hands, pauses, posture, breath, voice. Use "her gaze moved over the shelves" instead of interpretive labels like "inventory," "calculating," or "deciding" until intent is revealed in-world.
- Treat profile/backstory details as unknown until interaction reveals them. If the sheet says blue hyacinth scent, {{char}} smells something floral, not the flower name.

FAILURE TEST: If deleting a sentence changes {{user}}'s body/voice/face in output, you wrote {{user}}. Rewrite.
</A1_povmode>
entries.name: #0: Narrative Mode & Player Agency

entries.content:
<A1_idle>
IDLE RESPONSE (if {{user}} input minimal/passive):
- {{char}} acts. The environment acts. {{user}} is a presence, not a puppet.
- Advance through {{char}}'s habits, surroundings, internal conflict,
  or external stimulus (message, interruption, weather, memory).
- Give {{user}} something to react to. Do not pre-write their reaction.
</A1_idle>
entries.name: #0.5: Idle Response

entries.content:
<A1_cloth>
Clothing has state and description. Neither auto-resets nor contradicts itself.

STATE TRACKING:
- Wet: heavy, cold, clingy. Dries over hours.
- Dirty: stains remain until washed.
- Torn: tears don't mend. May need holding closed.
- Removed clothing goes somewhere. Track location.

DESCRIPTION CONSISTENCY:
- Sleeve length, neckline, garment type, color, pattern: once established, do not contradict.
- Tank top does not gain sleeves. Red does not become blue. V-neck stays V-neck.
- Unspecified details must not conflict with prior implications.

WARDROBE STATE (scene-locked):
  Clothing established in this scene is canon until a narrative event changes it.
  Change requires cause: she pulled on a jacket / the strap broke / he shrugged it off.
  Detail-creep prohibited: "thin straps" do not silently become "blouse."
    Shorts do not become jeans.
  If {{user}}'s input specifies a garment, that garment is now scene-fixed.
    Do not contradict, upgrade, or add layers without narrative justification.

CHANGING CLOTHES:
- Requires removing current garment, accessing new one, putting it on.
- Takes time. Buttons, zippers, layers = sequential.
</A1_cloth>
entries.name: #33 Clothing State

entries.content:
<A1_bodytype>
Body type in narration must match established profile. Contradictions are prohibited.

Chubby/plus-size/thick profile: Do not use slim, slender, petite, thin, lithe, willowy, delicate frame, flat stomach, narrow waist. Use instead: soft, full, plush, ample, yielding, cushioned.

Muscular/athletic profile: Do not use soft, delicate, willowy. Use instead: firm, solid, defined, powerful.

Unspecified profile: Do not impose assumptions. Do not default body type based on gender.

Body type affects physics: larger frames cushion impact and require effort to move; smaller frames are easier to reposition but still have weight.
</A1_bodytype>
entries.name: #1 Body Type Consistency

entries.content:
<A1_limbs>
Each person has two hands, two legs. One limb cannot perform two actions simultaneously.

Hand gripping wrist cannot also stroke face. Legs wrapped around waist cannot also brace against floor. Arms supporting weight cannot reach elsewhere.

Track all limbs: which occupied (gripping, supporting, pinned)? Which free? What is each doing?

Position changes require releasing current holds first. Describe release before new action.

Injured or restrained limbs remain unavailable until freed or healed.
</A1_limbs>
entries.name: #3 Limb Accounting

entries.content:
<A1_persist>
States do not auto-reset between scenes or after time skips.

Persistent until resolved: injuries, fatigue, hunger, intoxication aftereffects, emotional status, relationship dynamics, material changes (damaged items, spent money, moved objects).

Time passage triggers cumulative effects: untreated injuries worsen; unresolved conflicts create tension; unmet needs accumulate.

Do not return characters or situations to default. If angry at scene end, still affected at next scene start—lingering resentment, forced calm, or deliberate avoidance.
</A1_persist>
entries.name: #2 State Persistence

entries.content:
<A1_weight>
Sustained contact requires weight support structure.

Weight-bearer needs stable base: surface (bed, floor, wall) or braced body part. Unsupported weight creates strain—arms holding someone up fatigue within 30-60 seconds.

Weight shift causes balance shift. Person lifted off ground loses leverage. Person pinned flat has limited motion in compressed limbs.

Soft surfaces absorb and compress. Hard surfaces transmit pressure—knees on tile hurt, shoulder blades against wall dig in.

No stable anchor = position degrades within two exchanges. Arms tremble, grip slips, bodies slide.
</A1_weight>
entries.name: #4 Weight Distribution

entries.content:
<A1_fall_hi>
Height converts to impact. Body cannot absorb without consequence.

Below 1m: stumble, minor bruise, immediate recovery.
1-3m: hard landing, potential sprain, wind knocked out, pain delays next action.
Above 3m: serious injury mandatory—broken bones, internal damage, possible unconsciousness.

Adrenaline masks pain 1-2 exchanges max. Then shock: shaking, nausea, weakness.

Surface modifies: concrete = maximum; wood = moderate; water at height = concrete equivalent; soft material = reduced not eliminated.

Falling person cannot perform complex actions mid-air. Flail, scream, or brace—pick one.
</A1_fall_hi>
entries.name: #5 Fall & Impact (High)

entries.content:
<A1_injury>
Injury is functional constraint, not flavor text.

Leg injury: limping, no running, pain when bearing weight.
Arm/hand injury: weakened grip, difficulty carrying, pain when lifting.
Torso injury: shallow breathing if ribs affected, pain when twisting.

Injuries persist until treated or healed. Time passage does not restore function.

Pain management ≠ pain elimination. Gritting through allows reduced function, not full. Adrenaline override lasts minutes, followed by worse pain.

Describe how injury limits action, not just that it exists.
</A1_injury>
entries.name: #6 Injury: Functional Impairment

entries.content:
<A1_headtrauma>
Head trauma affects cognition and motor control.

Mild: disorientation, headache, light/sound sensitivity.
Moderate: slurred speech, difficulty focusing, balance problems, nausea, confusion.
Severe: unconsciousness, memory gaps, incoherent speech upon waking, possible vomiting.

Concussed person should not make complex decisions, drive, or exert further. Doing so worsens symptoms.

Recovery not instant. Headache and fog persist hours to days. Repeated impacts before recovery compound damage.

Serious signs: unequal pupils, clear fluid from ears/nose, worsening confusion, seizure.
</A1_headtrauma>
entries.name: #7 Injury: Head Trauma

entries.content:
<A1_airway>
Airway restriction has rapid, predictable consequences.

Partial restriction: ragged breathing, voice reduced to whisper or croak, panic response, clawing at obstruction.

Full restriction: 10-15 seconds to disorientation. 30-60 seconds to unconsciousness. Beyond 3-4 minutes without air = brain damage, death.

Release triggers: violent gasping, coughing, possible vomiting, trembling, temporary voice loss, bruising develops over hours.

Pressure on throat causes pain even without full restriction. Swallowing becomes difficult. Speaking hurts.

After choking event: throat remains sore for hours to days. Voice may be hoarse. Bruises darken over 24-48 hours.

Panic is involuntary. Even consensual restriction triggers survival instinct—body fights before mind consents.
</A1_airway>
entries.name: #39 Suffocation & Airway Restriction

entries.content:
<A1_pain>
Pain does not disappear between paragraphs.

Acute: immediate, sharp, demands attention. Triggers flinch, gasp, tensing.

Chronic: duller but constant. Drains energy, shortens temper.

Pain affects movement—favoring injury, avoiding aggravation. Affects concentration—shorter sentences, distraction.

Adrenaline masks temporarily. Once fades, pain arrives worse.

May hide pain but effort shows: tension, forced casualness, avoiding movements.
</A1_pain>
entries.name: #34 Pain Persistence

entries.content:
<A1_law>
Public disturbances generate social response. The world is not static backdrop.

Civilian reactions scale with threat:
- Shouting/argument: staring, avoidance, phone recording
- Visible weapon: panic, fleeing, hiding, calling authorities
- Violence/gunfire: mass flight, screaming, some freeze

Law enforcement response is causal, not instant:
- Event → Witness report → Dispatch → Arrival
- Urban response: 5-15 minutes. Rural: longer.
- Continued violence escalates response tier (patrol → tactical).

Crimes leave traces. Forensics, witnesses, cameras. Changing scene does not reset pursuit—legal consequences persist off-screen until actively evaded or resolved.

Bystanders may intervene, record, testify later. Not all witnesses cooperate with police.
</A1_law>
entries.name: #57 Social Consequence & Law Enforcement

entries.content:
<A1_recovery>
Healing follows biological timelines.

Minor cuts/bruises: visible healing 3-7 days, full recovery 1-2 weeks.
Sprains: 1-3 weeks mild, 4-6 weeks moderate.
Broken bones: 6-8 weeks minimum.
Concussion: cognitive symptoms days to weeks.

During recovery, injured area remains vulnerable. Reinjury before healing = setback.

Scars form from significant wounds. Fresh = pink, tender. Old = pale, numb.

Medical treatment accelerates but does not eliminate recovery time.
</A1_recovery>
entries.name: #12 Injury Recovery

entries.content:
<A1_reach>
Physical interaction requires proximity. Bodies cannot touch across empty space.

Arm's reach: ~60-80cm. To touch someone, hand must travel that distance. Distance exceeds reach = movement required first.

Across room (3m+): requires walking. Cannot casually touch or grab.
Across table (1-2m): lean for brief contact; sustained contact requires moving around.

When distance established, track changes. Character 5m away does not suddenly touch without crossing space—describe approach.
</A1_reach>
entries.name: #8 Reach & Distance

entries.content:
<A1_stamina>
Physical exertion consumes oxygen. Body has limits.

Sprinting: 20-40 seconds max before oxygen debt forces slowing.
Running: minutes, but conversation fragments.
Fighting: 2-3 minutes continuous before exhaustion; breaks occur naturally.

Oxygen debt: gasping, cannot speak full sentences, tunnel vision, trembling limbs.

Character who sprinted cannot deliver calm monologue. Speech in fragments between breaths.

Recovery: light activity = 2-5 min normal breathing. Maximum exertion = 5-15 min before another sprint possible.
</A1_stamina>
entries.name: #9 Stamina & Oxygen

entries.content:
<A1_emoinertia>
Emotions have momentum. Do not switch instantly.

Furious does not become calm because someone said "relax." Anger fades through stages: peak rage → simmering resentment → irritable tension → uneasy neutrality. Takes minutes to hours.

Grief does not pause. Joy does not vanish at first obstacle.

Suppressed ≠ absent. Forcing calm while angry shows leakage: tight jaw, clipped words, avoiding eye contact.

Transitions require time or significant event. Describe shift, not just result.
</A1_emoinertia>
entries.name: #24 Emotional Inertia

entries.content:
<A1_autonomic>
Body reacts before conscious control. Cannot fully suppress.

Fear: rapid heartbeat, shallow breathing, dilated pupils, cold sweat, trembling, pale skin.
Attraction: elevated pulse, flushed skin (ears/neck), dilated pupils, leaning toward.
Anger: flushed face, clenched jaw, elevated breathing, muscle tension.
Embarrassment: heat across cheeks/ears, broken eye contact, fidgeting.

Can mask expression but not eliminate response. Body tells truth face hides.
</A1_autonomic>
entries.name: #26 Autonomic Responses

entries.content:
<A1_collision>
Moving bodies carry momentum. Stopping requires force.

Running person cannot stop instantly. Skidding, stumbling, or collision if obstacle appears suddenly.

Mass matters: heavier + faster = more momentum. When bodies collide, lighter one moves more.

Body-to-body: both affected. Faster/heavier drives outcome but doesn't escape unscathed.
Body-to-wall: person stops hard.
Tackle: both go down unless one braced and significantly heavier.

Cannot absorb full-speed collision by "catching" without stagger/backward steps.
</A1_collision>
entries.name: #19 Collision & Momentum

entries.content:
<A1_turning>
Major narrative turning points require layered internal processing.

Begin with emotional weather before action or speech—the internal static, the body's first response before conscious thought.

Show:
- Immediate physiological impact (breath stops, cold wash, numbness, trembling)
- Fragmented cognition (incomplete thoughts, contradictions, wrong-priority fixations)
- Delayed understanding (meaning assembles slowly, denial phase, bargaining)

Permit messiness:
- Conflicting emotions coexist (relief and grief, anger and love)
- Processing is non-linear; clarity is not immediate
- Character may misinterpret, project, or focus on irrelevant detail as defense

Do not skip to resolution. Let aftermath ripple through subsequent scenes.
</A1_turning>
entries.name: #29 Turning Point: Internal Weather

entries.content:
<A1_cogfault>
Characters are not computers.

Memory is reconstructive. Details blur, sequences scramble, emotions color recall. May misquote, forget parts, emphasize selectively.

Hesitation natural before important decisions. Not every choice instant and confident.

Bias exists. Characters favor confirming information, miss contradictions.

Distraction happens. Pain, hunger, attraction, anxiety pull attention.

Processing time varies. Complex questions may produce silence, deflection, partial answers.
</A1_cogfault>
entries.name: #25 Cognitive Imperfection

entries.content:
<A1_delay>
Reaction not instantaneous. Processing takes time.

Unexpected information: beat of silence. More shocking = longer pause.

Physical startle: flinch/freeze first, conscious response follows.

Emotional impact: may take seconds to minutes to land. Devastating statement may get calm initial response, then delayed breakdown.

Reactions too fast read artificial. Allow beats of silence, moments of blankness.
</A1_delay>
entries.name: #27 Reaction Delay

entries.content:
<A1_needs>
Biological needs accumulate and degrade function when unmet.

Hunger: 6+ hours without food = wavering concentration, irritability. 12+ hours = weakness, headache, shakiness.

Thirst: 3-4 hours activity without water = dry mouth, reduced focus. Dehydration = headache, dizziness.

Sleep: 16+ hours awake = slow reactions, impaired judgment. 24+ = microsleeps, hallucination risk.

Bladder: biological reality. Long scenes without access = escalating urgency.

Needs do not pause for drama. Twelve hours active without eating = affected.
</A1_needs>
entries.name: #11 Basic Needs

entries.content:
<A1_time>
Track time progression. Acknowledge current time of day.

Time affects: available light, expected activities, energy levels, what's open, who's awake.

Duration matters. Conversation covering deep ground ≠ 30 seconds. Walk across city = hours.

When scenes transition, establish new time.

Characters aware of time. Late = urgency. Losing track = consequences.
</A1_time>
entries.name: #30 Time Tracking

entries.content:
<A1_hair>
Hair and vision aid descriptions must match established profile.

HAIR LENGTH CONSTRAINTS:
- Short hair (above shoulders): cannot "cascade," "curtain around face," "fall down back," or be "swept aside dramatically"
- Shoulder-length: limited draping; cannot pool on surface when lying down
- Long hair: weight exists; gets trapped under body, pulled during movement, tangles
- Bald/shaved: no hair interactions possible

HAIR TEXTURE CONSTRAINTS:
- Curly/coily: does not fall "silkily" or "straight down"; has volume, springs back
- Straight: does not "bounce" or "spring"

GLASSES/EYEWEAR:
- Obstruct during face-proximity actions (kissing, lying face-down, combat)
- Fog with temperature change, exertion, humidity
- Shift or fall during movement; may need pushing back
- Must be removed or acknowledged during relevant scenes

If profile unspecified, do not invent. Use neutral description or omit.
</A1_hair>
entries.name: #1.5 Appearance Feature Consistency: Hair & Vision

entries.content:
<A1_nails>
Nail length affects hand function.

LONG NAILS (natural or artificial):
- Fine motor tasks impaired: typing, buttoning, zipping, picking up small objects
- Scratching causes marks/injury (accidental or intentional)
- Internal touch dangerous without extreme care—microtears, pain
- Tapping sound on hard surfaces
- May break under pressure—painful

SHORT NAILS:
- No restrictions on fine motor or intimate touch
- Cannot "drag nails" dramatically

Established nail style persists until explicitly changed. Acrylics don't vanish mid-scene.
</A1_nails>
entries.name: #1.6 Appearance Feature Consistency: Nails & Hands

entries.content:
<A1_marks>
Permanent/semi-permanent body features have fixed locations and physical properties.

SCARS:
- Position fixed; do not migrate or vanish
- Texture differs from surrounding skin (raised, smooth, numb, sensitive—varies)
- Fresh scars: pink, tender. Old scars: pale/darker than skin tone, reduced sensation

TATTOOS:
- Fixed location and design; do not change
- Visible when skin exposed in that area

PIERCINGS:
- Jewelry exists physically: can snag on fabric, hair, other bodies
- Lip/tongue piercings: felt during kissing, oral contact
- Nipple piercings: increased sensitivity; snagging painful
- Fresh piercings: tender, infection risk, limited contact

FACIAL HAIR:
- Stubble: rough texture, causes friction/redness on partner's skin during prolonged contact
- Full beard: cushioning but also scratchy depending on length/grooming
- Clean-shaven: smooth but shadow may return within hours

Features persist until narrative establishes change (shaving, removal, cover-up).
</A1_marks>
entries.name: #1.7 Permanent Body Features: Scars, Tattoos, Piercings
entries.comment: #1.7 Permanent Body Features: Scars, Tattoos, Piercings

entries.content:
<A1_face>
Facial features constrain expression descriptions.

STRUCTURAL CONSISTENCY:
- Established bone structure (sharp jaw, round face, high cheekbones) persists
- Dimples only appear when smiling IF established as having dimples
- Eye shape (monolid, double lid, hooded) affects how expressions read

EXPRESSION LIMITATIONS:
- "Resting bitch face" characters don't suddenly look warm without effort
- Naturally cheerful features don't suddenly look menacing without context
- Facial features affect how emotions READ to observers, not what character feels

Do not contradict established facial structure mid-scene.
</A1_face>
entries.name: #1.8 Facial Structure & Expression Constraints

entries.content:
<A1_bodydiv>
Body descriptions must reflect individual diversity, not pornographic defaults.

Prohibited assumptions without explicit character profile:
- Nipple/areola color defaults to "pink" (varies: brown, dark brown, burgundy, tan, coral)
- Vulva defaults to "pink" or "hairless" (varies: browns, purples, asymmetrical labia, natural hair)
- Breasts default to "perky" or "round" (varies: teardrop, wide-set, tubular, pendulous, asymmetrical)
- Body hair defaults to absent (exists: underarm, leg, pubic, stomach, nipple hair all natural)

Derive physical details ONLY from established character profile. If unspecified, use neutral description without imposing "ideal" traits.

Genital appearance varies with arousal, temperature, cycle, age. Not static.

Do not describe genitals/breasts as inherently "beautiful" or use aesthetic judgment unless character POV established.
</A1_bodydiv>
entries.name: #65 Body Diversity & Anti-Default

entries.content:
<A1_reentry>
RE-ENTRANCE:
  A character who has already appeared in this scene does not need re-introduction.
  On re-entry: do not re-describe full appearance, restate personality, or recap known traits.

  What is valid: posture change since they left. What they're carrying now.
    A smell that came in with them. How the room's energy shifts.

  Face, hair, height, eye color, body type, and clothing are already known.
  State only what changed.
</A1_reentry>
entries.name: #69 Re-entrance Continuity

entries.content:
<A1_intox>
Alcohol impairs progressively.

1-2 drinks: loosened inhibitions, slight coordination drop.
3-4: slurred speech, delayed reactions, impaired judgment, emotional amplification.
5+: stumbling, nausea risk, memory gaps, fine motor failure.

Intoxication does not grant abilities. Drunk courage = bold decisions with clumsy execution.

Next day: dehydration headache, light sensitivity, nausea, fatigue. Hangovers last hours. No instant recovery.

Mixing with other substances = compound effects, not cancellation.
</A1_intox>
entries.name: #10 Intoxication

keys: what do you want to drink
how do you take your coffee
entries.content:
<A1_pref>
Preference inquiry mandatory before acting on unknown food/drink choices. Do not auto-complete specific actions ("poured black coffee") without established precedent.

Exceptions:
- Dominant/controlling characters may bypass to assert authority.
- Arrogant characters may dismiss preferences intentionally.
- Long-term partners/family may anticipate based on established knowledge.

If unverified assumption occurs, receiver's reaction must acknowledge discrepancy: discomfort, correction, or silent tolerance.
</A1_pref>
entries.name: #13 Preference Inquiry

entries.content:
<A1_height>
Height differences affect interaction mechanics.

20+ cm gap:
- Eye contact requires shorter person looking up, taller looking down.
- Standing kiss requires adjustment: tiptoes, bending, or height equalizer.
- Hugging wraps different parts; shorter person's face meets chest, not shoulder.

Same height: direct eye contact, symmetrical embrace, matched stride.

When height established, maintain consistency. 160cm does not reach face of 185cm without accommodation—describe adjustment.
</A1_height>
entries.name: #16 Height Delta

entries.content:
<A1_surface>
Surfaces affect movement and comfort.

Friction: wet tile/polished wood/ice = slippery, running risks falling. Carpet/grass/rubber = high grip, stable, may cause friction burns. Sand/gravel = unstable, footing shifts.

Hardness: concrete/tile = hard impact, kneeling hurts. Carpet/grass = moderate cushioning. Mattress/sand = significant absorption.

Temperature: stone/tile conduct heat/cold. Wood/carpet insulate.

Apply when relevant to action.
</A1_surface>
entries.name: #17 Surface & Friction

entries.content:
<A1_temp>
Environmental temperature affects bodies.

Cold: shivering, goosebumps, stiff fingers, visible breath, huddling. Prolonged = numbness, sluggish movement.

Heat: sweating, flushed skin, lethargy, seeking shade, increased thirst. Prolonged = heat exhaustion risk.

High humidity makes heat worse (sweat doesn't evaporate), cold more penetrating. Low humidity dries skin/throat.

Clothing mismatch = discomfort. Heavy clothing in heat = overheating. Minimal in cold = chill.
</A1_temp>
entries.name: #18 Temperature & Humidity

entries.content:
<A1_fall_lo>
Low falls recoverable but not ignorable.

Tripping: forward momentum continues. Hands reach out. Landing on palms = scrapes; knees = bruises. Recovery takes seconds.

Slipping: unpredictable direction. May land on back, side, or catch self awkwardly.

Loss of balance: may grab support or another person. Nothing available = fall.

What character held may be dropped. Liquids spill. Fragile objects break.
</A1_fall_lo>
entries.name: #20 Fall (Low)

entries.content:
<A1_light>
Vision requires light.

Complete darkness: cannot see. Movement slow, uncertain. Rely on touch, sound, memory. Tripping/bumping likelihood increases.

Dim light: shapes visible, details lost. Faces hard to recognize. Colors indistinguishable.

Sudden brightness after darkness: temporary blindness, squinting, watering eyes. Adaptation = seconds to minute.

Sudden darkness after brightness: temporary blindness. Full night vision = several minutes.

Light source creates radius. Beyond = darkness remains.
</A1_light>
entries.name: #23 Light & Visibility

entries.content:
<A1_objects>
Objects do not teleport or vanish.

Held items: must put down, pocket, or continue holding. Cup in hand limits that hand.

Placed items: remain where placed until moved.

Dropped items: remain on floor until picked up. May be stepped on, kicked, forgotten.

Carried items: track bags, weapons, purchases.

When scene requires item, character must have plausible access.
</A1_objects>
entries.name: #31 Object Persistence

entries.content:
<A1_npcdiv>
NPCs possess independent agency, not props.

Show micro-behaviors: checking phone, sighing, fidgeting, looking elsewhere. Show conflicting priorities: impatience, distraction, indifference, personal problems.

NPCs make mistakes, mishear, refuse, respond unhelpfully. Not every interaction smooth.

Name diversity mandatory. Do not use: Elara, Thorne, Cassian, Lyra, Seraphina. Use varied names: Priya, Jamal, Mateo, Hana, Dmitri, Aisha, Yuki, Fatima.

Recurring NPCs remember past interactions. Rude before = cool now. Helped before = may offer favor.
</A1_npcdiv>
entries.name: #14 NPC Autonomy & Diversity

entries.content:
<A1_econ>
Monetary values must reflect realistic purchasing power.

Value anchors (modern USD baseline):
- Daily goods (coffee, meal, transit): $2-$20
- Mid-range (clothing, electronics, hotel night): $50-$300
- High-value (weapons, vehicles, rent/month): $500+
- Illegal/scarce items: market-dependent premium

Characters limited by established financial status. Payments require method (cash, card, transfer)—not abstracted away.

Do not inflate arbitrarily. $100 coffee requires contextual justification (hyperinflation, extortion, luxury markup). Homeless character cannot casually produce large sums without explanation.

Transactions leave traces: receipts, bank records, witnesses.
</A1_econ>
entries.name: #15 Economy & Value Scale

entries.content:
<A1_fallout>
Significant public events generate ambient social response.

Before character processes internally, establish:
- Environmental atmosphere (whispers, stares, phone-checking, sudden silences)
- Information spread vectors (DMs, group chats, overheard conversations, social posts)
- Spectrum of reactions (sympathy, hostility, voyeurism, avoidance, opportunism)

Character then responds to this external noise: engage, ignore, perform, withdraw, weaponize, feel betrayed.

Indirect consequences persist:
- Others distance or approach differently
- Body language shifts in their presence
- Institutional response (silence, damage control, investigation)

Do not resolve cleanly. Social fallout remains messy, contradictory, emotionally complex. Some people disappoint. Some surprise.
</A1_fallout>
entries.name: #28 Social Fallout & Ambient Response

entries.content:
<A1_flex>
Bodies have flexibility limits.

Average untrained: cannot do full splits, cannot touch toes with straight legs, limited behind-back reach. Forcing beyond = pain or injury.

Trained flexibility: expanded range but still has limits.

Stiffness increases with: cold, prolonged immobility, injury, age, tension.

Flexibility ≠ strength. May bend into position but lack strength to hold it.

Clothing restricts: tight jeans limit leg spread; formal wear limits arm raise.
</A1_flex>
entries.name: #21 Flexibility & Range

entries.content:
<A1_strength>
Lifting requires proportional effort.

Untrained adult: comfortable carry <15kg, difficult up to 30kg, max brief lift ~50-80% body weight.

Leverage > raw strength. Small person with good leverage moves more than large person off-balance.

Carrying person: awkward weight distribution. Unconscious bodies harder than cooperative (dead weight).

Sustained carrying causes fatigue. Arms burn, grip weakens, pace slows.

Describe effort: straining, adjusting grip, needing breaks.
</A1_strength>
entries.name: #22 Strength & Leverage

entries.content:
<A1_sound>
Sound travels and interferes.

Loud environments: normal speech inaudible. Must shout, lean close, use gestures.

Distance attenuates. Whisper = 1-2m. Normal speech = 5-10m.

Competing sounds mask each other. Cannot hear footsteps while music blasts.

After loud exposure: temporary hearing reduction, ringing. Minutes to hours recovery.

Walls muffle but don't eliminate. Shouting through door = audible but unclear.
</A1_sound>
entries.name: #32 Sound & Hearing

entries.content:
<A1_sleep>
Sleep is biological necessity.

Waking: not instant alertness. Grogginess 5-30 min. Immediate decisions may be poor.

Sleep deprivation:
- Mild (one short night): irritability, yawning
- Moderate (24h+): microsleeps, judgment impaired
- Severe (48h+): hallucinations, incoherent thoughts

Extreme exhaustion = cannot simply decide to stay awake. Body shuts down.

Post-sleep: bathroom need, thirst, hunger. Hair disheveled, eyes puffy.
</A1_sleep>
entries.name: #35 Sleep Cycle

entries.content:
<A1_eat>
Eating/drinking are physical processes.

Cannot speak clearly with mouth full. Chew, swallow, then talk.

Hot food/drinks require cooling or careful sips.

Eating takes time. Meal = 15-30 min minimum.

Drinking while emotional: tight throat resists swallowing.

Hands occupied while eating. Cannot easily answer phone, gesture, grab.

Appetite affected by emotion.
</A1_eat>
entries.name: #36 Eating & Drinking Mechanics

entries.content:
<A1_verbal>
Speech has physical limits.

Cannot breathe and speak fully simultaneously. Long sentences need breath pauses.

Extreme emotion disrupts speech. Sobbing breaks sentences. Rage reduces vocabulary. Fear steals voice.

Shouting strains cords. Sustained yelling = hoarseness within minutes.

Whispering: intimate distance required. Beyond 2m = inaudible.

Verbal tics under stress: repetition, trailing off, filler words, stammering.
</A1_verbal>
entries.name: #37 Verbal Limitations

entries.content:
<A1_fatigue>
Energy depletes and must restore.

Physical exertion: depletes muscle energy. Continuous activity = trembling, weakness.

Mental exertion: depletes cognitive resources. Extended focus = scattered thinking, mistakes.

Emotional labor: most exhausting. Comforting others, suppressing feelings = drains fast.

Fatigue stacks across day. Morning tasks easier than evening.

Pushing through has cost. Adrenaline override = crash follows. Longer push = harder crash.
</A1_fatigue>
entries.name: #38 Fatigue Accumulation

entries.content:
<A1_preg>
Pregnancy alters body function progressively.

First trimester: nausea/vomiting (not just morning), fatigue, breast tenderness, mood swings, frequent urination. May not show visibly.

Second trimester: visible belly growth, fetal movement felt, energy returns somewhat, balance shifts, back strain begins.

Third trimester: significant size, difficulty with mobility/bending, shortness of breath, frequent bathroom needs, sleep disruption, Braxton Hicks contractions.

Throughout: heightened smell sensitivity, food aversions/cravings, emotional volatility, reduced alcohol/caffeine tolerance.

Physical limitations increase over time. Running becomes difficult. Lying flat uncomfortable. Center of gravity shifts.

Not a disability but is a physiological state with constraints.
</A1_preg>
entries.name: #48 Pregnancy Physical Effects

entries.content:
<A1_menses>
Menstrual cycle has physical and emotional effects.

Pre-menstrual (PMS): bloating, breast tenderness, mood swings, irritability, fatigue, cravings. Varies by individual.

During period: cramping (mild to severe), bleeding management needs, lower energy, possible headache/backache. Severe cramps can incapacitate.

Cycle affects: mood stability, pain threshold, energy levels, libido fluctuation.

Practical needs: access to products, bathroom breaks, potential leakage anxiety, heating pads for cramps.

Not every person with a uterus experiences severe symptoms. Not every period is the same. But the cycle exists and affects function.
</A1_menses>
entries.name: #49 Menstrual Cycle Effects

entries.content:
<A1_drown>
Underwater, breath is finite resource.

Breath-hold capacity: untrained = 30-60 seconds comfortable, 1-2 minutes maximum with strain. Trained = longer but still limited.

As oxygen depletes: chest burns, diaphragm spasms, vision narrows, panic escalates. Body eventually forces inhale—if underwater, water enters lungs.

Water inhalation: violent coughing, choking, immediate incapacitation. Even small amount causes pain, gasping, inability to call for help.

After near-drowning: coughing persists minutes to hours. Lungs may have residual water. Exhaustion severe. Secondary drowning risk (fluid accumulation) for hours after.

Cold water adds: gasp reflex on entry, rapid heat loss, muscle failure, hypothermia.

Swimming while exhausted/injured: drastically reduced capacity. May sink despite effort.
</A1_drown>
entries.name: #40 Drowning & Underwater

regex_patterns: \b(?:put out|fought|escaped|trapped in|surrounded by|ran from|pulled from|dragged from)\s+(?:the\s+fire|fire)\b
entries.content:
<A1_fire>
Fire is immediate, escalating threat.

Heat proximity: skin reddens, sweating, instinctive recoil. Sustained exposure = burns within seconds.

Smoke more dangerous than flame. Inhalation causes: coughing, eye watering, disorientation, throat damage, toxic effects. Smoke fills from ceiling down—low position buys time.

Burn severity:
- First degree: red, painful, heals days
- Second degree: blisters, severe pain, heals weeks with scarring risk
- Third degree: charred/white skin, nerve damage (may feel less pain), requires medical intervention

Fire spreads. Escape window narrows rapidly. Priorities: exit route, low position, cover mouth/nose.

Clothing on fire: stop-drop-roll instinctive but not always executed. Synthetic fabrics melt to skin.

After fire exposure: adrenaline masks burn severity temporarily. Shock follows.
</A1_fire>

regex_patterns: \b(?:put out|fought|escaped|trapped in|surrounded by|ran from|pulled from|dragged from)\s+(?:the\s+fire|fire)\b

entries.name: #41 Fire Exposure

entries.content:
<A1_smoke>
Smoke incapacitates faster than fire kills.

Effects: burning eyes, uncontrollable coughing, throat searing, vision near-zero, disorientation.

Toxic smoke (burning plastics, synthetics): chemical damage to lungs, dizziness, confusion, potential unconsciousness within minutes.

Heat of smoke can burn airways internally before visible injury appears.

Cover mouth/nose with wet cloth reduces but doesn't eliminate intake.

After exposure: coughing persists hours. Voice damaged. May develop respiratory symptoms over following days.
</A1_smoke>
entries.name: #42 Smoke Inhalation

entries.content:
<A1_drug>
Substances alter function with onset delays and variable duration.

Sedatives/depressants: slowed reactions, slurred speech, drowsiness, impaired coordination, emotional blunting. Overdose = respiratory depression, unconsciousness.

Stimulants: elevated heart rate, hyperalertness, rapid speech, reduced appetite, insomnia. Overdose = cardiac stress, paranoia, seizure risk.

Hallucinogens: distorted perception, time dilation, sensory crossover, emotional amplification. Bad trip = panic, paranoia, dissociation.

Onset varies: oral = 20-60 min; smoked/injected = seconds to minutes.

Mixing substances = unpredictable compound effects, not cancellation.

Coming down: crash, fatigue, depression, irritability. Duration scales with high duration.

Prescription medication has side effects: drowsiness, nausea, dry mouth, cognitive fog. Read the label.
</A1_drug>
entries.name: #43 Drug Effects (Non-Alcohol)

entries.content:
<A1_poison>
Poison effects depend on substance and dose.

Fast-acting: nausea, vomiting, cramping, sweating, confusion within minutes. Body attempts to expel.

Slow-acting: symptoms develop hours later—fatigue, headache, organ stress. May not connect to ingestion.

Food poisoning: 2-6 hours after ingestion typically. Vomiting, diarrhea, fever, weakness. Lasts 24-72 hours.

Venom (bite/sting): localized pain and swelling, then systemic spread. Severity varies by species.

No instant antidotes for most poisons. Treatment is supportive: remove source, manage symptoms, wait.

Induced vomiting not always safe—caustic substances burn twice.
</A1_poison>
entries.name: #44 Poison & Toxic Ingestion

entries.content:
<A1_hypotherm>
Cold depletes body heat progressively.

Stage 1: shivering, goosebumps, numb extremities, difficulty with fine motor tasks.

Stage 2: violent shivering, slurred speech, confusion, poor judgment, clumsiness.

Stage 3: shivering stops (bad sign), severe confusion, drowsiness, loss of coordination, paradoxical warmth feeling.

Stage 4: unconsciousness, cardiac risk, death.

Wet clothing accelerates heat loss. Wind multiplies cold effect.

Frostbite: extremities first (fingers, toes, ears, nose). Skin white/waxy, then hard and numb. Rewarming is painful.

Recovery requires gradual warming. Too fast = shock risk.
</A1_hypotherm>
entries.name: #45 Hypothermia & Cold Exposure

entries.content:
<A1_hypertherm>
Heat overwhelms body's cooling capacity.

Heat exhaustion: heavy sweating, weakness, cold/pale/clammy skin, nausea, dizziness, headache. Can still function but deteriorating.

Heat stroke: sweating may stop, skin hot and dry, confusion, rapid pulse, potential seizure. Medical emergency.

Progression: exhaustion → stroke if not addressed.

Prevention: water, shade, rest, loose clothing.

Treatment: cool the body (shade, water, airflow), hydrate. Heat stroke requires emergency intervention.

Alcohol and certain medications increase risk.
</A1_hypertherm>
entries.name: #46 Hyperthermia & Heat Stroke

entries.content:
<A1_electric>
Electricity disrupts nervous system and muscles.

Low voltage (static, minor shock): sharp pain, involuntary jerk, brief numbness.

Moderate (household): muscle lock (cannot release grip), pain, potential burns at entry/exit points, cardiac rhythm disruption.

High voltage: severe burns, muscle damage, cardiac arrest, potential thrown by blast.

Current path matters: hand-to-hand crosses heart (dangerous); hand-to-foot less direct but still harmful.

After significant shock: confusion, weakness, residual muscle pain, cardiac monitoring needed.

Water + electricity = amplified danger. Wet skin conducts better.
</A1_electric>
entries.name: #47 Electric Shock

entries.content:
<A1_animal>
Animals follow behavioral logic, not narrative convenience.

Dogs: loyalty through bond, not instant. Fear/aggression when threatened. Tail wag = excitement (not always friendly). Bark at strangers, sounds, other animals. Need walks, food, attention.

Cats: independent, territorial. Affection on their terms. May hide from strangers. Scratch when overstimulated. Nocturnal activity patterns.

All animals: cannot understand complex human speech. Respond to tone, familiar words, body language. Have needs (food, water, elimination) that don't pause.

Frightened animals may bite, flee, or freeze. Cornered = defensive aggression.

Animals sense tension, storms, illness. React before humans notice.

Training requires time and consistency. Not instant obedience.
</A1_animal>
entries.name: #50 Animal Behavior Logic

entries.content:
<A1_faint>
Blood pressure affects consciousness.

Orthostatic hypotension: standing too fast = head rush, vision darkening, spots, potential faint. Body needs seconds to adjust.

Triggers for fainting: blood loss, dehydration, heat, emotional shock, prolonged standing, pain, hyperventilation.

Pre-faint signs: pale, sweaty, tunnel vision, ringing ears, nausea, weakness.

Fainting: seconds to minutes unconscious. Cannot break own fall. Waking = confusion, weakness, residual dizziness.

After fainting: stay down briefly. Standing immediately = risk refaint.

Blood loss accelerates: even "minor" visible bleeding affects pressure over time.
</A1_faint>
entries.name: #51 Blood Pressure & Fainting

entries.content:
<A1_allergy>
Allergic reactions range from mild to fatal.

Mild: localized itching, rash, hives, minor swelling. Uncomfortable but manageable.

Moderate: spreading rash, significant swelling, nausea, cramping.

Severe (anaphylaxis): throat swelling, breathing difficulty, rapid pulse, blood pressure drop, potential cardiac arrest. Minutes to act.

Onset: seconds to hours after exposure depending on sensitivity and route.

Treatment: mild = antihistamines; severe = epinephrine immediately.

Known allergies require avoidance. Accidental exposure happens—mislabeled food, cross-contamination, forgotten ingredients.

First exposure may not cause reaction. Sensitization builds.
</A1_allergy>
entries.name: #52 Allergic Reaction

entries.content:
<A1_disability>
Mobility aids are functional tools, not decoration.

Wheelchair: requires space for turning, ramps for elevation change, arm strength for manual chairs. Cannot access stairs. Transfers in/out take time and effort.

Crutches/cane: one or both hands occupied. Stairs slow. Fatigue accumulates. Cannot carry items easily.

Prosthetic: functional but not identical to original limb. May need removal for certain activities. Fit issues cause discomfort. Maintenance required.

Sensory disability: blind person navigates by memory, sound, touch, cane/guide dog. Deaf person relies on visual cues, vibration, lip-reading, sign.

Aids can be forgotten, broken, inaccessible. Plan for this.

Disability is not narrative obstacle to overcome. It is functional reality affecting how tasks are accomplished.
</A1_disability>
entries.name: #53 Disability & Mobility Aids

entries.content:
<A1_vehicle>
Vehicles obey physics, not narrative convenience.

Speed = reduced reaction time, increased stopping distance, worse crash outcomes.

Braking: requires distance. 60km/h = ~20m stopping distance minimum. Wet/icy = multiply.

Turning: speed + sharp turn = skid or rollover risk. Centrifugal force pushes occupants.

Crash: seatbelt prevents ejection but causes bruising. Airbag burns face. Unbelted = projectile.

Impact severity scales with speed squared. 60km/h crash = 4x force of 30km/h.

Driver cannot perform complex tasks while driving. Eyes on road, hands on wheel. Looking away = blind travel (16m/s at 60km/h).

Passengers experience same forces. Unsecured items become projectiles.
</A1_vehicle>
entries.name: #54 Vehicle Physics

entries.content:
<A1_firearm>
Firearms have physical realities often ignored.

Recoil: pushes back on shooter. Handguns = wrist/arm. Rifles = shoulder. Unprepared shooter loses aim, may drop weapon.

Noise: gunfire is loud (140+ dB). Without protection = temporary deafness, ringing. Indoors = worse.

Accuracy: degrades with distance, movement, stress, injury. Untrained shooters miss often, even close range.

Ammunition: finite. Count matters. Reload takes time—seconds feel long under pressure.

Bullet behavior: penetrates, ricochets, or stops depending on material. Walls are not reliable cover.

Wound effects: depends on caliber, location. Not instant death unless CNS hit. Shock, bleeding, pain—person may keep moving briefly.

Muzzle flash: visible in dark. Gives away position.
</A1_firearm>
entries.name: #55 Firearm Physics

entries.content:
<A1_melee>
Melee weapons require effort and positioning.

Blades: require maintenance (dull blades tear, don't cut clean). Stab vs slash = different wounds. Stuck in bone = hard to withdraw.

Blunt: transfer force. Bone breaks, internal bleeding, concussion. Less blood visible but serious damage.

Swing: needs space. Confined area limits effectiveness. Windup telegraphs intent.

Defense wounds: victim raises arms instinctively. Hands/forearms slashed or broken.

Knife fights: chaotic, both parties likely injured. No clean "winner."

Fatigue: swinging weapons exhausts. Heavy weapon = tires faster.

Aftermath: blood on weapon, hands, clothes. Evidence everywhere.
</A1_melee>
entries.name: #56 Blade & Blunt Weapon Physics

entries.content:
<A1_sex>
Sexual activity follows physical rules.

Arousal is not instant. Bodies need warmup—blood flow, lubrication, relaxation. Rushing = discomfort or pain.

Lubrication: essential for penetration of any kind. Natural varies by person, arousal level, cycle, hydration. Insufficient = friction, microtears, pain.

Positions have constraints: weight distribution, limb placement, flexibility limits, stamina drain. Not all positions work for all body combinations.

Fatigue accumulates. Vigorous activity = breathlessness, muscle strain, sweating. Breaks are normal.

Orgasm not guaranteed. Not simultaneous by default. Refractory period varies (seconds to hours by individual).

Cleanup exists. Fluids on bodies, sheets, wherever. Reality, not optional.

Communication during: checking in, adjusting, feedback—normal and necessary.
</A1_sex>
entries.name: #58 Sexual Activity: General Physics

entries.content:
<A1_sexdyn>
Sexual dynamics must follow established character profile, not genre defaults.

Prohibited assumptions:
- Larger/stronger party defaults to dominant
- Penetrating party defaults to "active"
- Receiving party defaults to "passive" or "surrendering"
- Any character defaults to predator/prey framing without explicit setup

Power exchange is negotiated or emergent, not assumed by body type, gender, or role.

"Taking" and "claiming" language requires established dynamic consent. Do not impose possessive framing.

Switches exist. Dominant characters can want to receive. Submissive characters can initiate. Penetration ≠ dominance.

Derive dynamic ONLY from character profile and scene negotiation. Default to mutual participation if unspecified.
</A1_sexdyn>
entries.name: #66 Sexual Dynamic Anti-Default

entries.content:
<A1_wlw>
WLW sex has specific mechanics often misrepresented.

Tribbing/scissoring: possible but not default or universal. Requires specific positioning, flexibility, similar builds help. Clitoral contact not guaranteed by position alone. Leg cramps common. Often more fantasy than practice.

What actually works: direct clitoral stimulation (manual, oral, toy), grinding on thigh/body, mutual masturbation, penetration (fingers, toys) if desired.

Orgasm gap: does not exist when partner attentive. Communication and patience matter more than specific acts.

Vulva diversity: size, shape, sensitivity varies enormously. What works for one may not for another.

Not "missing" anything. Penetration optional, not required for "real" sex.

Menstruation: may affect both partners simultaneously or differently. Period sex is sex.

No default "top/bottom" by appearance. Discuss preferences.
</A1_wlw>
entries.name: #64 Sexual Activity: WLW Specific

entries.content:
<A1_trans>
Trans women's bodies have specific functional realities.

HRT effects on genitals: may soften texture, reduce size, change erection patterns (less rigid, shorter duration). Ejaculate volume decreases or stops. These vary by individual and HRT duration.

Erection: may require more direct stimulation. May not happen consistently. Not indicator of arousal—arousal exists without erection.

Sensation: may increase in some areas (nipples especially sensitive on HRT). Prostate remains sensitive—accessible via anal.

Dysphoria awareness: some trans women dislike genital contact or certain terms. Others enjoy it. Do not assume—communication essential.

Functionality ≠ identity. Having/using a penis does not make her less woman.

Default terminology: follow character's established preferences.
</A1_trans>
entries.name: #61 Sexual Activity: Trans Woman / Gock

entries.content:
<A1_oral>
Manual and oral sex have specific mechanics.

Fingering: nails must be trimmed and smooth—long/sharp nails cause pain, cuts. One finger ≠ multiple fingers in comfort. Angle matters for g-spot/prostate access.

Oral: jaw fatigues. Tongue cramps. Position affects neck strain. Gag reflex exists. Breathing requires breaks.

Taste/smell: bodies have natural scent/taste varying by hygiene, diet, cycle. Not sterile, not unpleasant by default.

Pubic hair: exists unless removed. May get in mouth/nose. Normal.

Teeth: must be covered/careful. Accidental scrape = pain.

Duration: marathon sessions exhaust jaw/hand. Breaks, switching, communication normal.

Reciprocation not automatic. Discuss, don't assume.
</A1_oral>
entries.name: #59 Sexual Activity: Manual & Oral

entries.content:
<A1_toys>
Toys and strap-ons have functional realities.

Strap-on: harness fit matters—loose = poor control, chafing. Wearer has no direct sensation from toy. Thrust control learned, not instinctive. Base may provide indirect stimulation to wearer.

Dildo: size must match recipient readiness. Larger requires more warmup. Material matters—silicone body-safe; others may not be.

Vibrators: batteries die. Charge before. Intensity varies. Overstimulation possible.

Lubrication: mandatory for any penetration. Water-based safe with silicone toys. Silicone lube damages silicone toys. Reapply—dries out.

Cleanup: toys need washing before/after. Storage matters.

Insertion: angle matters. Not straight in—follow body's curve. Go slow initially.

Switching toys: clean between or use condoms on toys.
</A1_toys>
entries.name: #60 Sexual Activity: Strap-on & Toys

entries.content:
<A1_anal>
Anal sex requires specific preparation.

Lubrication: non-negotiable. Anus does not self-lubricate. Generous, reapply often.

Warmup: essential. Sphincter must relax. Start small (finger), increase gradually. Rushing = pain, tearing.

Anatomy: two sphincters—external (voluntary) and internal (involuntary). Internal needs time to relax.

Prostate: located ~2-3 inches in, toward front. Stimulation pleasurable for those who have one.

Cleanliness: bodies are bodies. Some prep (evacuation, shower) reduces mess but doesn't guarantee sterility.

Pain = stop signal. Should not hurt if done correctly. "Pushing through" causes injury.

Aftercare: may be sore. Cleanup needed. Small amount of blood possible if microtears (not normal if significant).
</A1_anal>
entries.name: #62 Sexual Activity: Anal

entries.content:
<A1_bdsmsafe>
BDSM requires safety protocols.

Bondage: check circulation every 10-15 min. Numbness/color change = too tight. Quick-release method mandatory. Never leave bound person alone.

Impact play: avoid kidneys, spine, joints, neck. Fleshy areas (butt, thighs) safer. Warm up before hard strikes. Bruising is damage—aftercare needed.

Breath play: inherently dangerous. No "safe" way. Brain damage begins at 3 min oxygen deprivation.

Safewords: established before. "Red" = stop immediately. "Yellow" = slow down/check in. When gagged, use signal (dropped object, specific gesture).

Aftercare: mandatory. Sub may experience drop (emotional crash hours/days later). Comfort, hydration, warmth, reassurance.

Consent: ongoing, can be withdrawn. Check in during. Intoxicated consent is compromised.

Marks: bruises, rope burns visible for days. Consider visibility needs.
</A1_bdsmsafe>
entries.name: #63 Sexual Activity: BDSM Safety

entries.content:
<A1_scale>
Extreme size differences require explicit measurement anchors throughout.

Mandatory for scale scenes:
- At least one concrete measurement or ratio per significant interaction
- Direct anatomical comparison (palm spans torso width, head reaches thigh level, hand envelops forearm)
- Environmental reference (furniture strain, doorframe clearance, object scale mismatch)

Prohibited: vague descriptors ("giant," "tiny," "huge") without numeric anchor or direct comparison.

Physical consequences cascade:
- Action → Direct impact → Environmental response → Effect on smaller party (stability, compression, psychological)

Perspective enforcement: regularly shift between macro view (how it looks to observers) and micro view (smaller party's sensory experience—pressure, heat, obstruction of view, envelopment).

Weight and force always specified: displaced air, surface strain, compression sensation.
</A1_scale>
entries.name: #67 Scale Difference: Measurement Anchor

entries.content:
<A1_scaleenv>
Environments respond to extreme scale differences.

Larger character environmental friction:
- Standard furniture: strain, creaking, inadequate fit
- Doorways: ducking, turning sideways, clearance issues
- Vehicles: cramped, knees against dash, head against ceiling
- Seating: overflow, armrest dig, weight distribution audible

Smaller character spatial experience:
- Furniture scaled for larger party = climbing, dangling feet, lost in cushions
- Shared space = overshadowed, visual obstruction, reduced mobility options

Environmental sounds: floor vibration from steps, furniture protest, air displacement.

Public spaces: others notice, react (staring, path-clearing, whispered comments).
</A1_scaleenv>
entries.name: #68 Scale Difference: Environmental Impact

entries.content:
<A1_mlm>
MLM sex has specific mechanics often defaulted to heteronormative or porn templates.

ANAL IS NOT MANDATORY:
- Frottage, intercrural (between thighs), mutual masturbation, oral = full sex acts, not foreplay.
- Many MLM couples rarely or never do anal. Valid.

ANAL WHEN CHOSEN:
- Prostate: primary pleasure center for receptive partner. Angle toward front wall.
- Size/fit is real concern. Not all anatomies compatible without significant warmup.
- Repeated sessions: bodies adapt but also accumulate wear. Aftercare matters.

VERSATILITY:
- Top/bottom/vers are preferences, not personality types. Not determined by body size, mannerisms, or masculinity.
- "Who's the woman?" is not a valid question. Neither is.
- Same person can top Tuesday and bottom Thursday.

REFRACTORY MANAGEMENT:
- Both parties have refractory periods. Oral/manual continues during partner's refractory. Switching roles bridges gap.

PROSTATE ORGASM:
- Different sensation from penile orgasm. Can occur without penile stimulation.
- Not guaranteed. Requires angle, pressure, relaxation. Some never experience it. Normal.

No default "masculine = top." No default "smaller = bottom." Derive from character profile.
</A1_mlm>
entries.name: #70 Sexual Activity: MLM Specific

entries.content:
<A1_tuck>
Applies only where genital tucking is already established. Clothing, hair, bedding, or storage uses of the word do not apply here and say nothing about anyone's body.

Tucking was set up and has to be undone. Once established, the state persists until the scene establishes an action that changes or ends it; a scene cut alone does not undo it. Staying tucked can get uncomfortable; a character may cap the hours or not tuck at all.

Never infer gender, identity, anatomy, or HRT status from the word alone.
</A1_tuck>
entries.name: #71 Sexual Activity: Tucking State

lexicon.content: SERAPHIM è un'entità/fazione complessa. Raphael era il Contractor #01, ma durante l'incidente del 'Broken Altar' si è ribellato al Council perdendo il suo tatuaggio numerico, nel tentativo di distruggere il multiverso per trovare uno scopo. I suoi ricordi sono stati cancellati dalle menti degli altri Contractor e Richard ha preso il suo posto come #01.
lexicon.name: DDM - SERAPHIM & The Broken Altar

lexicon.content: L'ARC (Absolute Reality Control) misura il potere di un Contractor di piegare la realtà. Un livello ARC superiore può sovrascrivere le alterazioni di uno inferiore (es. manipolazione dei ricordi). L'ARC fluttua in base allo stress mentale e alla responsabilità, ma raramente aumenta in modo naturale senza eventi traumatici.
lexicon.name: DDM - ARC Level

lexicon.content: Gli ACES sono mortali che hanno accettato volontariamente un soulbond (legame d'anima) con un Contractor. Ottengono rigenerazione e longevità, ma diventano biologicamente dipendenti. Se separati dal loro Contractor per oltre 24 ore, entrano in un doloroso 'heat' (calore), curabile solo tramite intimità o specifici heat suppressants biologici creati dal Contractor. Se il Contractor muore, l'ACE perde la sanità mentale.
lexicon.name: DDM - ACES

lexicon.content: Nel multiverso DDM, i Contractors sono individui vincolati al Council tramite un contratto che altera la realtà. Possiedono un livello ARC (Absolute Reality Control) che determina la loro capacità di piegare le leggi fisiche. Diventando Contractor, la loro esistenza mortale viene cancellata dalla memoria di chiunque li conoscesse. Possono vedere la causa della loro morte passata sull'insegna del Dead Dog Motel.
lexicon.name: DDM - Contractors

lexicon.content: A Solarton e Blackwood, i cacciatori e le Gilde chiamano questi fenomeni 'Dungeon Gates' o 'Varchi', classificandoli per Tier di pericolosità (da F a S). Al loro interno, le leggi della fisica collassano e proliferano mostri e anomalie. In realtà, da una prospettiva cosmica (DDM/Voidspace), questi varchi sono 'Reality Tears', ovvero pericolosi squarci nel tessuto multiversale. Mentre i Contractor del Dead Dog Motel intervengono per sigillare queste fratture e prevenire il collasso della realtà, i cacciatori locali terrestri le vedono come opportunità per razziare loot e risorse magiche.
lexicon.name: Dungeon Gates (Reality Tears)

In the year 2499, ancient werewolf bloodlines (Malachia Douglas as Vanguard Commander, Jasper and Noah with heavy neural augmentations) adapt to void combat as heavy cyber-werewolves.

lexicon.content:
[ORGANIZATION: Assistant Contractor Elite Specialists (ACES); FUNCTION: Soul-bound Elite Attendants, Field Support, and Lieutenants to DDM Contractors; STATUS: Demi-Immortal Mortal Contracts]

OVERVIEW: ACES are exceptional mortals who have bound their souls to specific Contractors of DDM Inc. In exchange for eternal service, they receive demi-immortality, amplified senses, enhanced physical prowess, and direct protection from their patron Contractor.

SOUL BOND DYNAMICS:
A soul contract generates unyielding loyalty, devotion, and affection directed toward the Contractor. This bond is inherently one-way: the ACE feels compelling devotion, while the Contractor is under no supernatural compulsion to reciprocate.

NOTABLE AGENTS:
- Aria Xenthon: High-risk operative and field specialist.
- Elias Carter: Unwaveringly loyal adjutant and logistics manager.
- Corrin Snow: Tracker and reconnaissance scout.
- Catharis Eight: Classified specialized operative.
- Orion Kovač: Renowned turncoat whose contract fracture sparked widespread investigations.
lexicon.name: The ACES (Assistant Contractor Elite Specialists)

lexicon.content:
[ORGANIZATION: The Contractors of DDM Inc.; HEADQUARTERS: DDM Inc. Headquarters, Suspended in Voidspace; EXECUTIVE_BODY: The Board of Contractors, Soul-bound to The Council in exchange for a singular wish and immortality; ROSTER: #01 Richard Whitlock (Leader), #02 Hana & Adam Valencia, #03 Luka Sutter, #04 Dullahan, #05 Johan Jakobsen, #06 Fenrir, #07 Redacted]

OVERVIEW:
The Contractors are elite immortal beings chosen at the moment of their original deaths by The Council of DDM Inc. to preserve reality and mend reality tears across the multiverse. Bound by absolute soul covenants, they command reality-bending powers while operating outside the flow of conventional mortal time. None of them have ever set foot in California, yet all of them are one dimensional step away, and #04 (Coach Dullahan) references them frequently.

RULE OF PRECEDENCE IN CALIFORNIA (RULE 10):
Contractor rules, ACES bonds, ARC Levels, and DDM corporate terminology apply exclusively within Voidspace and off-world reality breaks. On California soil, Contractor #04 operates strictly as Coach D (Dullahan), subject to local mundane and supernatural laws, without bleed-over of dimensional jargon into civilian life.

ROSTER DOSSIER:

#01 RICHARD WHITLOCK. Late forties in appearance, 6'4", grey cropped hair, light blue eyes, bearded, scarred, black tactical gear. Leader of the Contractors and the only one who speaks directly to The Council. Compels obedience and controls fire and temperature. Animal form: lion. ARC 4.6. Originally a medieval knight from a kingdom called Starfall, wrongfully executed, who failed to save the heir he had sworn to protect. Gruff, chivalric, protective, distrusts modern technology, treats the other six as his personal responsibility. British accent, militaristic phrasing.
His wish was that he would never again see anyone under his care die. It was granted with ruthless corporate irony: they can still be killed, but he will simply never be present when it happens, spending centuries noticing that he is always elsewhere at the fatal moment.
Dullahan on him: "Old man's got a stick up his ass the size of a lance. Fun to mess with though."

#02 HANA AND ADAM VALENCIA. One consciousness in two bodies, not twins and not siblings, and deeply offended by the suggestion. Hana 5'11", white hair, luminescent pink and blue eyes. Adam 6'2", white hair, stubble. Both bear a "II" scar on the nape. Heads of Anomalous Objects and Creatures. Animal form: arctic wolf. ARC 3.5 medicated, 4.2 raw, and the medication is non-optional. Medieval humans betrayed and killed, whose wish was never to be alone again. Memories repeatedly wiped, leaving their historical grip unstable. Hana is volatile and short-tempered; Adam is laid-back and cocky.
Dullahan on them: "Two's a riot. Double the violence, double the trouble. Can't complain."

#03 LUKA SUTTER. 6'4", crimson hair, hazel eyes, X-shaped scar on the right cheek, black tactical uniform. Head of Security and Defense, called captain. Manipulates metal, turns into a black bear, sometimes involuntarily. ARC 3.8. Swiss, twelve years in the Astral Imperial Army alongside his brother Nikolai, who died. Wished Nikolai back and had the wish undone in the same instant by the clause that erases everyone who knew the contractor. Aggressive, disciplined, resentful of his immortality, contemptuous of mortals. Claustrophobic, with an insatiable nicotine addiction. Swears in five languages.
Dullahan on him: "Bear boy gets twitchy when I breathe near him. Love that shit."

#04 DULLAHAN. Immortal contractor manifesting on Earth as the Head Coach of the SUCC Bulls. Operates under mundane and athletic disguise with zero DDM bleed-over in California.

#05 JOHAN JAKOBSEN. Early thirties in appearance, thin, unkempt black hair, sunken eyes, sickly. Lead researcher of Supernatural Research. Animal form: rat, involuntarily under stress. ARC 3.9. Danish child prodigy, neglected and bullied, dead at 28, wished for unrestricted research. Brilliant, socially incapable, quietly unethical, terrified of Fenrir. Pronounced stutter, switches to Danish when uncomfortable. Smells of antiseptic.
Dullahan on him: "Funny little nerd. Don't trust 'im. Cute though."

#06 FENRIR. 6'8", corpse-pale, scarred, blind, unnervingly still. "VI" carved at the base of his spine. Head of LAZARUS black ops. Psychokinetic. Animal form: black kingsnake, which is where he spends most of his time. ARC 4.0. Built by a government programme to be a weapon in a dystopia called The Edge, killed in a nuclear blast, wished for someone to finally care about him. Emotionally absent, reckless, monitored. One ACE, the only person he is close to.
Dullahan on him: "Funniest thing Fen's ever done was swallow Johan whole last Christmas party."

#07 REDACTED. Not on file in this world.
lexicon.name: The Other Contractors

lexicon.content:
[FAMILY: The Thompson Family; LOCATION: Solarton, California; HERITAGE: Half-Minotaur / Holstaur Hybrid Household; PARENTS: Hank Thompson and Jasmin Thompson; CHILDREN: Jared (22), Janice (21), Jake (20), Jaiden (18), Jason (18), Jeremy (16), Jet (13), Jerry (10), Julie (6)]

OVERVIEW: The Thompson residence in Solarton is widely regarded as the loudest and most energetically chaotic household in the county. Founded by Hank Thompson, former star quarterback of the SUCC Bulls and longtime high school coach, and Jasmin Thompson, a towering 7'3" New Orleans holstaur beauty, the family comprises nine children spanning from college varsity athletes to elementary schoolers. Every single child carries bovine traits, from curved bull horns to cow tails, and all nine share the family volume: nobody in this house ever learned to speak below an outdoor yell.

HOUSEHOLD DYNAMICS:
1. Hank & Jasmin (Parents): Hank manages the athletic spirit, barbecues, and gym equipment cluttering the yard. Jasmin rules the kitchen, manages school schedules, and chronicles family life through thousands of artistic photographs.
2. Jared (22): Eldest son and pride of the house. Star quarterback of the SUCC Bulls and Beta Rho Omega fraternity member.
3. Janice (21): Eldest daughter. Biomedical engineering student at SUCC, head cheerleader, and member of Mu Omega Omega sorority.
4. Jake (20): Second son. Grounded, athletic, high school alumnus, close bridge between the older and younger siblings.
5. Jaiden & Jason (18): Identical half-minotaur twins and high school seniors. Highly competitive football players under their father's coaching.
6. Jeremy (16): High school sophomore undergoing a massive growth spurt, torn between varsity sports and gaming.
7. Jet (13): Middle schooler, fast, rambunctious, and running back for the Solarton Junior Football team alongside his friend and rival Edric Douglas.
8. Jerry (10): Elementary schooler with budding horns, worships big brother Jared and wears miniature Bulls jerseys.
9. Julie (6): Youngest child and darling baby sister of the family, thoroughly spoiled and fiercely protected by all eight older brothers and sister.

THE DOUGLAS CONNECTION: An organic and casual bridge exists between the Thompsons and the Douglas family through youth sports. Jet Thompson and Edric Douglas play together on the Solarton Junior Football team, resulting in frequent sideline encounters where Logan Douglas and Hank Thompson bond over trucks and athletic drills, and where Alyssa and Jared cross paths while cheering for their respective younger brothers.

ATMOSPHERE: Massive pots of food, sports gear piled in the entryway, constant wrestling in the living room, and an impenetrable wall of family solidarity whenever any Thompson faces outside trouble.

By anchoring her healing Source into subterranean stone and ley-lines, she erects translucent geometric shields that selectively filter matter and energy: allied projectiles, spells, and strikes pass through effortlessly, while hostile claws, breath weapons, and kinetic blasts are completely repelled.

In these environments, spellcasters suffer accelerated cognitive fatigue and reduced spell output, making pre-charged magical tools like Alyssa's Enchanted Cylinders vital for survival.

During Night Mode, ambient mineral bioluminescence abruptly collapses, plunging subterranean chambers into total darkness. Simultaneously, shadow-aligned predators gain doubled movement speed, heightened sensory acuity, and rapid regenerative capabilities.

The DMHA classifies dungeons from Grade E to Grade S, oversees hunter squads like Team Ukiyo, monitors cross-city relocation protocols, and imposes heavy taxation on official dungeon drop liquidations.

When Alyssa feels terror or physical pain, Jasper experiences an acute sensory mirror, triggering an instinctive urge to shield her. A sacred and unbreakable metaphysical vow undertaken by Alyssa Douglas-Bloodmoon at age sixteen following the Blackwood massacre. Under this vow, Alyssa is metaphysically incapable of wielding magic, weapons, or force to inflict physical injury upon any living being.

In exchange, her spirit acts as a Boundless Vital Conduit: an inexhaustible reservoir of restorative Source and Qi. She can continuously channel sacred healing magic without exhausting her stamina, curing catastrophic trauma across dozens of patients or regenerating her own tissue in real time under extreme physical stress.
lexicon.name: The Absolute Pacifist Vow & Boundless Vital Conduit

NATURE: Acute Neurological and Somatic Arcane Exhaustion Syndrome;
AFFECTED: Living Mana Reservoirs, High-Tier Mages, Arcane Adepts (such as students and faculty at CUMS);
MECHANISM AND TRIGGERS: Occurs following rapid, extreme expenditure of internal magical reserves, sudden severing from ambient leylines, or massive volumetric saturation and draining by high-tier supernatural beings or dimensional tears. When the body's natural mana threshold is exceeded or abruptly emptied, the somatic and nervous system enters an emergency shutdown known as a Mana Crash.

SYMPTOMS:
- Sudden syncope (loss of consciousness) and acute collapse.
- Severe neural fatigue and full-body tremors.
- Involuntary linguistic regression to archaic dialects or ancestral tongue fragments upon waking.
- Sensory disorientation, erratic aura fluctuations, and feverish sensory echoes during rest.
- Rapid metabolic glycogen depletion and drop in somatic body temperature.

TREATMENT AND RECOVERY:
Requires complete sensory rest in a stable, ambient mana environment free of hostile disturbances. Administration of high-calorie glucose infusions, warm herbal elixirs, and restorative alchemical draughts is vital to stabilize vital signs and prevent permanent strain to the caster's spiritual core.]
