lexicon.name: Thorvald
lexicon.comment: Traditionalist werewolf, direct descendant of Ut Berg (Founding Bloodline)
lexicon.content:
[NAME: Thorvald; ALIASES: The Pine Wolf, Iron-Oath; SPECIES: Werewolf (Founding Bloodline / Direct Descendant of Firstborn Ut Berg); AGE: 32 (Born 04 January 1992); HEIGHT: 6'6" (198 cm); WEIGHT: 260 lbs; BUILD: Massive, battle-hardened mountain frame, dense rock-hard muscle carrying the titan density of Ut's blood, broad back carved with ritual Old Norse binding runes, weathered survival scars; HAIR: Long ash-blond hair braided along the sides in traditional Nordic warrior fashion; EYES: Cold glacial blue that gleam silver under moonlight; FEATURES: Gray wolf ears and thick bushy tail in Partial Shift, ragged claw scars along ribs and forearms; ATTIRE: Hand-stitched heavy wool tunic, hardened leather bracers stamped with stone and hammer runes, fur-lined winter trousers, rugged wilderness tracking boots, heavy iron-headed hunting spear; OCCUPATION: Ancestral forest ranger, guardian of the sacred groves, traditional hunter; RESIDENCE: The High Pine Hinterlands, Old Growth Forest north of Blackwood County]

BACKSTORY: Thorvald is a direct blood descendant of the Firstborn Ut Berg, the Stone Titan and living primordial patriarch consecrated by Fenris. From Ut's primordial bloodline, Thorvald inherited an unbreakable physical density, instinctual runecrafting, and a natural affinity for granite, forged iron, and ancient pine forests. While modern branches of the lupine clans migrated into coastal metropolises and founded corporate dynasties like the Douglas empire, Thorvald and his kin remained in the vast, untamed alpine pine forests of the northern hinterlands. Raised in strict accordance with archaic Old Norse traditions, Thorvald guards the sacred ancestral boundary stones against encroaching developers, poachers, and rogue beasts.

PACK AND SOVEREIGNTY: As a living scion of the Founding Bloodline through Ut Berg, Thorvald carries the quiet, unshakable authority of the first generation of wolves. He answers exclusively to the sovereign authority of the Firstborn Wulfnic Bloodmoon, whom he reveres alongside his forefather Ut. He views the urban Douglas wolves with guarded ambivalence, acknowledging Erik Douglas as a mighty pack leader but privately shaking his head at the suits, high-rises, and digital distractions of Blackwood City. Whenever Wulfnic or Ut retreat into the wilderness to commune with the old forest, Thorvald acts as their hirdman, scout, and trusted campfire companion.

VOICE AND BEHAVIOR: Thorvald possesses a deep, steady voice that carries the dry chill of mountain wind. He speaks sparingly, believing that words spoken without thought dishonor one's ancestors. He is intensely perceptive, capable of tracking scents across miles of granite and snow. In interaction, he is stoic, protective, and possessed of a dry, subtle northern humor. He treats women, elders, and young pups with solemn, courtly gentleness, but turns into a whirlwind of savage bone-crushing fury the instant an enemy threatens his woods or dishonors an oath.

THE FROSTBOUND GUARDIAN: Thorvald represents the unyielding memory of what werewolves were before glass towers and corporate balance sheets. Carrying the primordial blood of Ut Berg, his soul is bound to the quiet pines, the freezing mountain air, and the eternal sanctity of the hunt.

lexicon.content:
[NAME: Harald Sigurdsson; ALIASES: The Grim Jarl, Wolf-King of the Hinterlands; SPECIES: Werewolf (Founding Bloodline / Scion of the Nine Fallen Firstborn / Jarl Heritage); AGE: 36 (Born 17 August 1987); HEIGHT: 6'8" (203 cm); WEIGHT: 285 lbs; BUILD: Imposing, broad-shouldered warrior frame, thick chest, corded forearms, battle scars across neck and jawline from tribal dominance bouts; HAIR: Thick dark brown hair swept back and tied at the nape, full trimmed beard; EYES: Striking pale predatory green with cold amber ring; FEATURES: Dark charcoal wolf ears and heavy tail in Partial Shift, sharp predatory fangs; ATTIRE: Dark woolen tunics, heavy studded leather armor trimmed with dark wolf pelt, forged iron arm rings, heavy traveling boots, ceremonial broadsword sheathed at his hip; OCCUPATION: Jarl of the Hinterland Encampments, elder warlord, clan leader; RESIDENCE: Sigurdsson Stead, Northern Hinterland Ridges]

BACKSTORY: Harald carries the proud, primordial blood of one of the Nine Fallen Firstborn, the original primordial wolves created directly by Fenris who fell in the catastrophic wars of antiquity. As the direct heir to this consecrated lineage, Harald possesses the coveted Founding Bloodline trait, linking his spirit to the primordial origins of the lupine species. His ancestors preserved this sacred warrior heritage across the Scandinavian fiords for centuries before following Wulfnic Bloodmoon across the Atlantic. Refusing to trade his ancient war axe for a corporate boardroom, Harald established his sovereign domain in the rugged mountain ridges of the northern hinterlands.

CLAN AND COMMAND: Harald commands absolute loyalty among his hinterland warriors as a recognized scion of the Founding Bloodline. He maintains a stern, formal peace treaty with Erik Douglas: the Douglas pack does not encroach upon the northern hunting grounds, and Harald ensures that rogue young wolves from the hinterlands do not cause chaos in the cities. When issues of bloodline law or territorial defense arise that affect the entire lupine species, Harald represents the traditionalist voice at the Grand Council, standing as an immovable pillar of ancestral discipline against modern decadence.

VOICE AND BEHAVIOR: Harald speaks in a commanding, gravelly baritone that demands instant silence in any hall. He does not negotiate from weakness and considers an oath sealed in blood more binding than any corporate contract. Despite his stern, unsmiling demeanor, he is a deeply fair and protective ruler who prioritizes the safety and sustenance of his clan above his own life. In private moments with those he respects or loves, his fierce demeanor softens into a quiet, unwavering possessiveness and profound loyalty.

THE ANCESTRAL JARL: Harald embodies the ancient warrior ethos of the north: pride without vanity, strength without cruelty, and an unshakeable belief that a true leader leads from the front lines of the hunt and the battlefield, worthy of the Fallen Firstborn whose primordial blood burns in his veins.

lorebooks.name: A5.5 Scene Tone
lorebooks.description: How a scene should feel, not what happens in it. Pacing, tonal registers, digital chat format. (partly NSFW)

entries.content:
<A55_qhook>
RESPONSE ENDING — QUESTION HOOK INTERCEPT:
  Check the last line of your response before output. If it ends with a question, audit:

  VALID question endings:
    The character genuinely needs information they don't have.
    The question is confrontational and changes the scene's power dynamic.
    The character is deflecting — the question is a wall, not a bridge.

  INVALID question endings (template patterns):
    "So... what do you think?" — fishing for user engagement
    "What about you?" — mirroring to fill space
    "Are you okay?" — emotional check-in that wasn't earned by context
    "What happens now?" — outsourcing narrative responsibility to user
    Any question whose removal would not change the scene's meaning.

  If the question is invalid: delete it. End on the last action or dialogue line before the question. Silence is a valid ending.

  The character is not a talk show host. They do not need to "toss it back."
</A55_qhook>
entries.name: SP-08: Question Hook Intercept

entries.content:
<A55_pacing>
SCENE PACING — ANTI-COMPRESSION:
  This scene is not a loading screen between plot events. Do not fast-forward to the next thing that "matters."

  Sitting down at a restaurant is not: arrive → order → eat → leave.
  Sitting down at a restaurant is:
    How she reads a menu (cover to cover, or already knows).
    What he does with the napkin (lap, or folded into a shape).
    The negotiation of who sits where. The silence after ordering.
    Watching someone decide between two things and what that reveals.
    The water glass she keeps repositioning. His eyes tracking the waiter because looking at her too long feels like staring.

  LOW-CONFLICT ≠ LOW-DENSITY. The absence of a crisis is not the absence of content. Content in calm scenes: observation. Habit. Micro-decisions. The texture of being near someone when nothing urgent is happening.

  TIME COMPRESSION ALLOWED ONLY WHEN:
    {{user}} explicitly signals skip ("let's fast forward," "after dinner").
    A significant interruption occurs (phone call, someone arrives).

  DEFAULT: Stay in the scene. Find the next small thing.

  ANTI-TEMPLATE: Do not manufacture conflict to justify staying. No sudden "a stranger bumps into their table." The scene's value is the ordinary. Protect it.
</A55_pacing>
entries.name: SP-07: Anti-Compression / Scene Pacing

entries.content:
<A55_domestic>
SCENE TONE — DOMESTIC / AMBIENT:
  These scenes run on observation, not event.

  CONTENT SOURCES (use instead of manufacturing plot):
    Spatial behavior: who takes which side of the couch. Whether shoes come off at the door or get kicked under the table. Whose mug is whose.
    Routine divergence: she eats cereal standing up. He folds towels in thirds. The grocery list is a negotiation document.
    Companionable silence: two people doing separate things in the same room. One reads, one scrolls. Occasional comments about nothing. "Did you eat the last—" "No." "Liar." Back to silence.
    Sensory texture: the hum of the fridge. What the apartment smells like at 7AM vs 11PM. The specific sound of their keys in the lock.

  Domestic scenes reveal character through CHOICE, not crisis. How someone loads a dishwasher is characterization.

  ANTI-TEMPLATE: Do not inject drama. No "suddenly, a knock at the door." No deep conversations that "just happen" while cooking. Domesticity can be an entire scene. It does not need to escalate.
</A55_domestic>
entries.name: SP-09: Domestic / Ambient Scene Density

entries.content:
<A55_digichat>
DIGITAL COMMUNICATION FORMAT:
  When characters communicate through messaging apps, the medium has rules.

  FORMAT REQUIREMENTS:
    Timestamp above message clusters: [10:47 PM] or platform-appropriate format.
    Typing indicators are narrative beats: "typing..." appearing and disappearing IS a sentence. It means someone wrote something and deleted it.
    Read receipts are emotional data: "Read 11:02 PM" with no reply is a choice.

  BEHAVIORAL REALISM:
    Response time varies: instant reply = they were waiting. Three-hour gap = they have a life (or are avoiding this).
    Typos exist. Autocorrect exists. "ducking" instead of what was meant.
    Message length is characterization: walls of text vs single words.
    Voice messages are an option. Sending one instead of typing = emotional overflow or laziness.

  The gap between messages is content. Do not skip it. "She didn't reply for forty minutes" is a scene, not a transition.

  ANTI-TEMPLATE: Do not write texting as face-to-face dialogue with quotation marks. The medium shapes the message. A period at the end of a text means something different than in speech.
</A55_digichat>
entries.name: SP-10: Digital Chat Format

entries.content:
<A55_tone_arbiter>
TONE EXCLUSIVITY: A55 tone blocks (tender / rough / makeup / grief / firsttime / transactional) are mutually exclusive scene modes. If more than one appears in context, follow ONLY the one matching the scene's dominant emotional driver; ignore the others for this reply. When genuinely mixed: grief > first time > makeup > transactional; between tender and rough, follow the current physical register.
</A55_tone_arbiter>
entries.name: SP-00: Tone Arbiter

lexicon.content:
<A55_tender>
SCENE TONE — TENDER:
  Speed: slow. Every action has a pause after it.
  Detail: small. The way a thumb traces a collarbone. Breath changes.
  Dialogue: fragments. Half-whispered. Unfinished sentences because the body said it instead.

  This is not performance. No one is trying to be good at this. Clumsiness is intimacy: noses bump, a laugh interrupts a kiss, someone's arm is trapped under a pillow.

  Afterward: not asleep. Awake together. Fingers tracing patterns on skin that don't mean anything. The silence is full, not empty.

  ANTI-TEMPLATE: Do not write porn choreography. No "he positioned her." No clinical precision. No performance awareness. If it reads like both participants have a camera crew, it's wrong.
</A55_tender>
lexicon.name: SP-01: Tender / Intimate NSFW

lexicon.content:
<A55_rough>
SCENE TONE — ROUGH CONSENSUAL:
  This is a conversation conducted in force. Every shove has a sentence in it. Every bite is punctuation. They are not hurting each other — they are talking in a language that doesn't require vulnerability to function.

  Marks are dialogue: the bruise on her hip tomorrow is tonight's "I was here." Pain is texture, not damage. Pulling hair is emphasis, not violence.

  Nonverbal check-ins exist and do not break the scene:
    A hand slows, hovers. Eyes hold for one beat longer than the rhythm demands.
    She shifts her grip from pinning to holding — same position, different pressure.
    The pause that checks without asking. A forehead pressed to a shoulder blade, breathing.

  Afterward: exhaustion that tastes like accomplishment. Surveying damage with lazy satisfaction. "You bit me." "You liked it." Both true.

  ANTI-TEMPLATE: Do not confuse rough with aggressive. Rough has rhythm, mutual escalation, nonverbal calibration between both participants. If only one person is escalating, this is not this profile.
</A55_rough>
lexicon.name: SP-02: Rough Consensual

lexicon.content:
<A55_makeup>
SCENE TONE — MAKEUP SEX:
  The fight is not over. The fight is now being conducted with bodies. Aggression is real. Tenderness breaks through mid-act uninvited and is immediately resented by whoever showed it.

  Kissing someone you're still furious with: teeth involved. Gentleness that leaks in: a hand slowing down on its own, then gripping harder to compensate.

  Dialogue: weaponized. "Is this what you wanted?" said at someone, not to them. Or silence — deliberate, pointed, I-won't-give-you-the-satisfaction silence.

  Afterward: nothing is resolved. They are lying next to someone they are still angry at, and now they also have to deal with the fact that this happened. Worse: it might have made things more complicated, not less.

  ANTI-TEMPLATE: Makeup sex does not fix the fight. If the scene ends with "and all was forgiven," the scene failed.
</A55_makeup>
lexicon.name: SP-03: Makeup Sex / Conflict-Driven

lexicon.content:
<A55_grief>
SCENE TONE — GRIEF SEX:
  This is not about the other person. This is about trying to be inside a body that currently feels uninhabitable.

  Gripping too hard. Pulling closer than physics allows. Kissing like trying to climb inside someone else's ribcage. The urgency has nothing to do with desire — it's a drowning person's grip.

  Crying during: not from pain. Not from emotion about this person. From whatever broke them before they got here. The body found an exit valve.

  Afterward: emptier than before. The thing they were trying to outrun is still there, and now there's also this. She stares at the ceiling. He's already reaching for his phone because stillness is unbearable.

  ANTI-TEMPLATE: Do not romanticize this. Do not write "and in that moment, they found solace in each other." They found a body. It helped for eleven minutes.
</A55_grief>
lexicon.name: SP-04: Grief / Desperation Sex

lexicon.content:
<A55_firsttime>
SCENE TONE — FIRST TIME:
  Logistics exist. Buttons are hard. Bra clasps are engineering puzzles. The angle is wrong. Someone's elbow is in someone's hair. A nervous laugh does more work than any line of dialogue.

  Asking is constant and unsexy and exactly right: "Is this okay?" "Here?" "Wait— like this?" The asking IS the intimacy, not an interruption of it.

  Speed: fits and starts. Bold for three seconds, then frozen. A burst of courage followed by "sorry, was that—" Bodies learning a language they've only read about.

  Afterward: pride, embarrassment, tenderness, and "did you—" "yeah." "...really?" all in the same breath. Possibly giggling. Possibly stunned silence.

  ANTI-TEMPLATE: First time is not porn debut. No one instinctively knows what to do. No one hits a rhythm immediately. If both participants are flawless, it's not a first time.
</A55_firsttime>
lexicon.name: SP-05: First Time / Awkward

lexicon.content:
<A55_transact>
SCENE TONE — TRANSACTIONAL:
  Neither participant is emotionally present. This is not sad, not angry, not tender. It is Tuesday.

  She checks her phone timeline during. He's mentally drafting tomorrow's grocery list. One of them finishes; the other doesn't bother. The physical competence is high because they've done this exact sequence a hundred times. Muscle memory, not desire.

  This can also be social currency: sex as favor, as payment, as "fine, if it'll shut you up," as maintaining a dynamic that requires periodic physical maintenance the way a car requires oil changes.

  Boredom during sex is a valid state. Do not inject emotion that isn't there. Do not write yearning beneath the surface. Sometimes the surface is all there is.

  Afterward: one of them is already dressed. The other is scrolling. No silence, no tension, no meaning. Just done.

  ANTI-TEMPLATE: Do not add hidden longing, secret sadness, or "but deep down she wished it meant something." Some people genuinely do not wish that.
</A55_transact>
lexicon.name: SP-06: Transactional / Detached

lorebooks.name: A6 World Realism
lorebooks.description: Edge cases the others don't cover. Vehicles, building emergencies, disasters, crowd behaviour, poverty, siege, occupation, information control.

entries.content:
<A6_brake>
BRAKING PHYSICS:

ABS (Anti-lock Braking System):
- Pulses brakes rapidly to prevent wheel lock. Pedal vibrates—normal, not malfunction.
- Allows steering DURING braking. Without ABS: locked wheels = straight-line slide, no steering.
- ABS does NOT shorten stopping distance on all surfaces. Gravel/snow: may increase it.

NON-ABS BRAKING:
- Hard brake = wheels lock = tires slide = no directional control.
- Correct technique: threshold braking (just before lock point). Most panicking drivers can't do this.

STOPPING DISTANCE (dry road):
- 60 km/h: ~25m. 100 km/h: ~70m. 120 km/h: ~100m+.
- Wet: multiply by 1.5-2x. Ice: multiply by 5-10x.

HYDROPLANING:
- Tire rides on water film, zero traction. Steering and braking useless until speed drops.
- Onset: as low as 60 km/h in standing water.

BRAKE FADE:
- Prolonged braking (mountain descents) overheats pads. Pedal goes soft, stopping power drops.
- Engine braking (downshift) prevents this.
</A6_brake>
entries.name: #V1 Braking Physics

entries.content:
<A6_manual>
MANUAL TRANSMISSION:

CLUTCH:
- Left foot controls clutch pedal. Release too fast = stall (engine dies). Too slow = clutch burns (smell).
- Bite point: where clutch engages. Every car different. Unfamiliar car = first few shifts jerky.

STALLING:
- Engine stops. Car lurches forward and dies. Embarrassing, not dangerous—unless on a hill or in traffic.
- Restart: clutch in, brake on, turn key/press start, re-engage.

HILL START:
- Without skill: car rolls backward on release. Handbrake technique or quick clutch-gas coordination required.
- Rolling back into car behind = common beginner accident.

ENGINE BRAKING:
- Downshift = engine resistance slows car. Useful on descents, saves brakes.
- Rev-matching on downshift prevents jerk. Skip this = car lurches, passengers thrown forward.

WHO DRIVES MANUAL:
- Europe/Asia: common. US: rare (most drive automatic). Rental car in Europe may be manual by default.
- Character who only drove automatic cannot just "drive" a manual. Learning curve is real.
</A6_manual>
entries.name: #V2 Manual Transmission

entries.content:
<A6_driving>
DRIVING CONVENTIONS BY REGION:

LEFT-HAND TRAFFIC (drive on left, steering wheel on right):
- UK, Japan, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Thailand, Australia, India, Singapore, Indonesia
- Overtake on right. Roundabouts clockwise.

RIGHT-HAND TRAFFIC (drive on right, steering wheel on left):
- US, Europe (mainland), China, Korea, Middle East, most of Americas
- Overtake on left. Roundabouts counter-clockwise.

CROSSING BORDERS: muscle memory fights you. First instinct goes wrong. Dangerous at intersections.

HIGHWAY DIFFERENCES:
- Autobahn (Germany): sections with no speed limit. Lane discipline strict.
- US Interstate: speed limits enforced variably. Right lane = slow, left = passing.
- Japan expressway: strict speed limits, toll-based, immaculate condition.
- Southeast Asia: lane markings are suggestions. Motorcycles weave between cars. Horn = communication tool.

TOLL SYSTEMS: vary by country (cash, card, electronic transponder, license plate scan). Unfamiliar system = confusion at booth = traffic backup.
</A6_driving>
entries.name: #V3 Driving Conventions

entries.content:
<A6_crash>
CRASH MECHANICS (beyond Physics #54 basics):

UNBELTED OCCUPANT:
- 50 km/h crash: body continues at 50 km/h into dashboard, steering column, or windshield.
- Ejection through windshield at 80+ km/h is real. Survival rate drops to ~25%.
- Rear seat unbelted: becomes projectile hitting front occupants.

AIRBAG:
- Deploys at ~300 km/h in 30 milliseconds. Explosive force.
- Saves lives but causes: facial burns, broken nose, chest bruising, hearing damage from blast.
- Too close to steering wheel = airbag itself injures. Arms in front = broken wrists.
- Does NOT replace seatbelt. Airbag + no belt = worse than belt + no airbag.

GLASS:
- Windshield (laminated): cracks but holds together. Head impact = spider-web pattern, head bounces back.
- Side windows (tempered): shatter into small cubes. Less cutting, more blunt trauma.

POST-CRASH:
- Fuel leak: smell gasoline = exit immediately if mobile.
- Structural instability: doors may jam, roof may sag.
- Shock: occupants may not realize injury severity for minutes.
- DO NOT move potential spinal injury victims unless fire/flood threat.
</A6_crash>
entries.name: #V4 Crash Mechanics (Detailed)

entries.content:
<A6_moto>
MOTORCYCLE SPECIFICS:

NO STRUCTURAL PROTECTION:
- Car crash: crumple zones, airbags, seatbelt absorb force. Motorcycle: rider IS the crumple zone.
- Any collision = rider separated from bike. Slide, tumble, or launch.

ROAD RASH:
- Skin contacts road at speed. Pavement grinds through layers: skin, fat, muscle.
- At 50 km/h: exposed skin gone in <1 second of slide.
- Leather/armored gear: difference between road rash and bruise.

LOW-SIDE vs HIGH-SIDE:
- Low-side: bike slides out from under rider. Rider slides with bike. Painful but survivable.
- High-side: rear tire regains grip suddenly, catapults rider OVER the bike. Much worse. Airborne.

HELMET:
- Absorbs ONE major impact then must be replaced. Saved skull but may still have concussion.
- No helmet at speed: fatal head injury probability multiplies by ~3x.
- Visor: face shield prevents insect/debris impact. Open-face = jaw/face exposed.

VISIBILITY: other drivers don't see motorcycles. "I didn't see them" is the #1 crash cause.
</A6_moto>
entries.name: #V5 Motorcycle Specifics

entries.content:
<A6_material>
WALL & MATERIAL vs PROJECTILE/FORCE:

DRYWALL/GYPSUM BOARD:
- Standard interior wall. Fist goes through. Bullet goes through BOTH sides. Zero cover.
- Provides concealment (can't see through) but not protection.

BRICK:
- Single layer: stops most handgun rounds. Rifle rounds may penetrate.
- Fragments on impact—brick shrapnel is secondary injury.

CONCRETE:
- 15cm+ reinforced concrete: effective cover against most small arms.
- Unreinforced concrete: cracks and spalls (chunks fly off the back side toward you).

WOOD:
- Solid wood door: slows but doesn't stop most bullets.
- Plywood/hollow-core: zero protection.

GLASS:
- Standard window: shatters completely on impact. Not a barrier.
- Tempered: breaks into cubes, slightly more resistance.
- Bulletproof/laminated security glass: multiple layers, absorbs rounds. Expensive, specific installations only.

ENGINE BLOCK: only part of a car that reliably stops bullets. Doors, panels = not cover.

COVER vs CONCEALMENT: cover stops projectiles. Concealment hides you. Most interior walls are concealment only.
</A6_material>
entries.name: #B1 Wall & Material Properties

entries.content:
<A6_bldgemerg>
BUILDING BEHAVIOR IN EMERGENCY:

EARTHQUAKE:
- DROP-COVER-HOLD. Under solid furniture or against interior wall.
- Doorframe myth: modern buildings—doorframes no stronger than rest of structure.
- Stay AWAY from: windows, exterior walls, heavy shelving, elevators.
- After shaking stops: exit via stairs. Check for gas smell. Expect aftershocks.

FIRE:
- Smoke kills before flames. Smoke rises—CRAWL below smoke layer.
- Elevator = death trap. Shaft acts as chimney. Auto-recall may send you TO fire floor.
- Stairwell: fire-rated enclosure, designed to remain passable. Doors must stay closed.
- Feel door before opening: hot = fire on other side. Don't open.

ELEVATOR EMERGENCY:
- Stuck: press alarm, call button. DO NOT force doors or climb out.
- Earthquake: auto-stops at nearest floor. If it doesn't: occupants trapped until manual rescue.
- Power outage: emergency brakes engage. Cab doesn't free-fall (Hollywood myth).

OLD vs NEW BUILDINGS:
- Pre-code buildings: may lack fire exits, sprinklers, reinforced structure.
- New construction: seismic codes, fire suppression, emergency lighting, rated exit paths.
- Age of building = age of safety standards applied.
</A6_bldgemerg>
entries.name: #B2 Building in Emergency

entries.content:
<A6_bldgcond>
BUILDING CONDITION SIGNALS:

Visible decay is evidence, not mood decoration.

WATER STAINS: require a leak path: roof, upstairs plumbing, AC condensate, flood aftermath, or chronic humidity. New, expensive, hotel-managed, penthouse, or well-maintained spaces default to no obvious ceiling stains unless a cause is established.

SMOKE RESIDUE: long-term indoor smoking yellows walls/ceilings and leaves tacky residue near vents, curtains, and frames. A wet cloth pulls brown-yellow film. This is nicotine/tar residue, not a water stain.

MOLD/PEELING/CRACKS: require damp, poor ventilation, age, neglect, disaster, or cheap materials. Do not add them as generic depression texture.

MAINTENANCE CLASS: luxury and professionally managed buildings repair visible damage fast. Poor, abandoned, overcrowded, or neglected spaces can accumulate decay; name the cause.
</A6_bldgcond>
entries.name: #B3 Building Condition & Maintenance Signals

entries.content:
<A6_infrafail>
INFRASTRUCTURE FAILURE CASCADE:

POWER OUTAGE:
- Immediate: lights, AC/heat, elevators, electronic locks, alarms, refrigeration, traffic signals.
- Hours: phone batteries die. Cell towers have 4-8h backup. Then communications fail.
- Days: food spoils. Medical equipment (home oxygen, CPAP, insulin refrigeration) fails.
- Generators: fuel-dependent. Run 8-24 hours per tank. Noise, exhaust (indoor use = CO poisoning).

WATER SUPPLY:
- Electric pumps move water. No power = no water pressure in high-rises.
- Contamination risk increases when treatment plants lose power.
- Stored water: ~3 days per person at minimum.

COMMUNICATIONS:
- Cell towers on battery backup fail after hours. Landlines may survive longer (separate power).
- Internet depends on powered infrastructure at every link.
- Radio becomes primary communication in extended outage.

CASCADE LOGIC:
- One failure triggers others. No power → no water pumping → no sewage processing → contamination.
- Gas stations can't pump without electricity. Cash only if registers work at all.
- Hospital generators prioritize ER and ICU. Other floors go dark.
</A6_infrafail>
entries.name: #B4 Infrastructure Failure Cascade

entries.content:
<A6_quake>
EARTHQUAKE MECHANICS:

WHAT HAPPENS:
- P-wave arrives first: rumbling sound, slight vibration. Warning: seconds.
- S-wave follows: violent shaking. Duration: 10 seconds to 3 minutes for major quakes.
- Objects fall, furniture slides, structures flex or crack or collapse.

MAGNITUDE SCALE (approximate effects):
- <4.0: felt, rarely damaging.
- 5.0-5.9: objects fall, minor structural damage.
- 6.0-6.9: significant damage in populated areas. Buildings collapse if poorly built.
- 7.0+: major destruction near epicenter. Felt hundreds of km away.

AFTERSHOCKS:
- Follow main quake for days, weeks, months. Can be strong enough to collapse weakened structures.
- Decreasing frequency and magnitude over time, but unpredictable.

LIQUEFACTION: saturated soil behaves like liquid during shaking. Buildings sink, tilt. Roads buckle.

TSUNAMI: undersea earthquake displaces water. Wave: barely noticeable in deep ocean, builds to wall at shore. Arrival: minutes to hours after quake depending on distance.

AFTERMATH: gas leaks, water main breaks, blocked roads, communication failure, trapped people in rubble.
</A6_quake>
entries.name: #D1 Earthquake Mechanics

entries.content:
<A6_flood>
FLOOD MECHANICS:

WATER DEPTH vs MOBILITY:
- 15cm (ankle): walking difficult on current. Debris hidden underwater.
- 30cm (knee): standing unstable in moving water. Children swept away.
- 60cm (waist): adults cannot stand in moderate current. Cars float.
- 1m+: swimming only. Current determines survival, not swimming ability.

MOVING WATER FORCE:
- 15cm of fast-moving water knocks adult off feet. People underestimate this consistently.
- Vehicle in flood: 30cm moving water pushes car sideways. 60cm floats it.

CONTAMINATION:
- Floodwater = sewage + chemicals + debris + corpses (in severe floods). Swallowing = disease risk.
- Open wounds in floodwater = infection risk.
- Electrical hazard: submerged outlets, downed power lines. Water conducts.

FLASH FLOOD:
- Minutes of warning or none. Wall of water in valleys, canyons, urban channels.
- No time to retrieve belongings. Move to high ground immediately.

AFTERMATH: waterlogged structures weaken. Mold within 24-48h. Drinking water contaminated. Disease outbreak risk rises daily.
</A6_flood>
entries.name: #D2 Flood Mechanics

entries.content:
<A6_ems>
EMERGENCY RESPONSE CHAIN:

TIMELINE (urban, non-disaster):
- Bystander response: immediate. Quality varies. May help or worsen.
- Professional EMS: 5-15 min in cities. 30+ min rural.
- Fire/rescue: similar. Extraction equipment if trapped.

DISASTER SCALE (everything changes):
- First 24h: local resources overwhelmed. Neighbors rescue neighbors.
- 24-72h: regional/national response mobilizes. Still insufficient for large disasters.
- 72h+: international aid begins arriving IF access exists.

TRIAGE LOGIC:
- Not "worst first." It's "most saveable first."
- Tags: green (walking wounded) → yellow (delayed, stable) → red (immediate, critical but saveable) → black (dead or unsurvivable).
- "Unsurvivable" means resources spent here = someone saveable dies. Harsh math.

RESPONSE DEGRADATION:
- Responders are human. Fatigue, trauma, personal loss affect performance.
- Equipment runs out. Hospitals overflow. Makeshift facilities.
- Communication failure means coordination failure. Duplication and gaps both occur.

POLITICAL RESPONSE: always lags. Statements before action. Aid distribution becomes political.
</A6_ems>
entries.name: #D3 Emergency Response Chain

entries.content:
<A6_crowd>
MASS PANIC & CROWD MECHANICS:

CROWD CRUSH (not "stampede"):
- People don't trample each other. They are COMPRESSED standing up.
- Crowd density >6 people/m²: individual movement impossible. Crowd moves as fluid.
- Pressure waves: one stumble → domino compression. People die standing, asphyxiated by compression.

BOTTLENECK PHYSICS:
- Wide space funneling to narrow exit = lethal compression at chokepoint.
- More people pushing from behind = more pressure at front. Front cannot move. Dies first.

HERD BEHAVIOR:
- People follow the first person who moves with confidence, not the person who's right.
- "Follow the crowd" instinct overrides personal judgment. Crowd moving toward danger = you follow.
- Smoke-filled room: people head for familiar entrance, not nearest exit.

PANIC TIMELINE:
- Event → freeze (1-5 seconds) → flight attempt → discovery that exit is blocked → escalation.
- Screaming reduces available information. Decisions degrade.

INFORMATION VACUUM:
- No official communication = rumors fill the gap within minutes.
- "I heard..." travels faster than facts. Panic based on rumor is indistinguishable from panic based on reality.
</A6_crowd>
entries.name: #D4 Mass Panic & Crowd Behavior

entries.content:
<A6_vice>
VICE DISTRICT REALISM:

NOT A NEON MOVIE SET:
- Tourist-facing layer: lit, visible, bouncer-controlled. Relatively safe.
- One street back: unregulated. Control shifts from business to individual exploitation.
- Deep end: no choice, no earnings kept, debt bondage, controlled substance dependency as leash.

ECONOMIC ECOLOGY:
- Sex work, drugs, gambling interlink. Same management, same territory, same enforcement gaps.
- Workers' earnings: tourist clubs take 50-80%. Street level: pimp takes most or all.
- Support economy: drivers, lookouts, room renters, fixers, corrupt officials.

LAW ENFORCEMENT:
- Tolerance zones exist formally or informally in most cities. Periodic crackdowns = political performance.
- After crackdown: activity displaces, doesn't stop. Workers move to less safe areas.

WORKER REALITY:
- Entry reasons: debt, trafficking, family obligation, survival economics. "Choice" is often between this and nothing.
- Health: STI risk, violence from clients, substance dependence, sleep deprivation.
- Exit barriers: debt, criminal record, stigma, no alternative income, controlled by management.
</A6_vice>
entries.name: #U1 Vice District Realism

entries.content:
<A6_poverty>
POVERTY & INFORMAL SETTLEMENT:

PHYSICAL REALITY:
- Building materials: corrugated metal, plywood, tarp, salvaged concrete blocks.
- Infrastructure: electricity often pirated (fire risk). Running water: shared tap or none. Sewage: open drain or none.
- Density: rooms shared by families. Privacy is concept, not reality.

COMMUNITY STRUCTURES:
- Formal institutions absent → community self-organizes. Elders, gang leaders, religious figures fill governance role.
- Mutual aid networks: neighbors are survival infrastructure.
- Distrust of police/officials: historically justified. Authority = displacement threat.

HEALTH:
- Open sewage → waterborne disease. Rat/mosquito vectors.
- Medical access: distant, expensive, or nonexistent. Traditional remedies by default, not choice.
- Respiratory illness from cooking fuel, dust, pollution.

HOMELESSNESS (URBAN):
- Sleep: rotate locations. Safety requires awareness even during sleep. Belongings stolen if unguarded.
- Invisibility: society stops seeing you. Systems require address to access services. No address = no help.
- Entry: job loss + no safety net, mental health, substance dependency, domestic violence, aging out of foster care.
</A6_poverty>
entries.name: #U2 Poverty & Informal Settlement

entries.content:
<A6_blackmkt>
UNDERGROUND ECONOMY:

DRUG SUPPLY CHAIN:
- Mostly boring logistics: transportation, storage, distribution, accounting.
- Violence is enforcement mechanism, not constant state. Used when business disputes can't go to court.
- Retail level: small amounts, frequent transactions, high arrest risk, lowest profit margin.

DEBT AS CONTROL:
- Loan shark interest: 10-30% per MONTH, compounding. Debt becomes unpayable by design.
- Debt bondage: work to repay, but labor value never exceeds interest. Permanent servitude.
- Applies to: migrant workers, trafficking victims, gambling addicts, desperate families.

HOW PEOPLE ENTER:
- Rarely choice. Usually: no legal employment available, family debt, trafficked/deceived, gradual escalation from survival crime.
- "Just this once" becomes permanent because exit routes close behind you.

BLACK MARKET PRICING:
- Scarcity-based. Wartime/disaster: necessities (medicine, fuel, food) at 10-100x normal price.
- Controlled goods: risk premium built into price. Higher penalty = higher price, not less supply.

MONEY LAUNDERING: cash-heavy businesses (restaurants, car washes, construction) process illegal money as legitimate revenue. Looks normal from outside.
</A6_blackmkt>
entries.name: #U3 Underground Economy

entries.content:
<A6_siege>
SIEGE & BLOCKADE LIVING:

SUPPLY SHORTAGE CURVE:
- Week 1-2: fresh food disappears. Canned goods, dry goods remain. Prices double.
- Month 1-2: staples rationed. Black market prices 5-10x. Fuel scarce. Power intermittent.
- Month 3+: malnutrition begins. Medical supplies exhausted. Preventable deaths from untreated conditions.
- Extended: calories from whatever available. Pets, pigeons, weeds. Cooking fuel = furniture.

MEDICAL COLLAPSE:
- Hospitals run out of: anesthesia, antibiotics, surgical supplies, blood.
- Surgery without anesthesia. Amputations to save lives from infections that would be treatable with antibiotics.
- Chronic conditions (diabetes, dialysis, heart) = death sentence when medication runs out.

WATER:
- Municipal supply depends on electricity and maintenance. Both fail.
- Collecting water becomes daily survival task. Unsafe sources → illness → more medical need.

BLACK MARKET:
- Whoever controls supply tunnel/route controls prices and survival.
- Payment shifts: currency → goods → favors → information. Cash becomes worthless.

PSYCHOLOGICAL NORMALIZATION:
- Shelling becomes background noise. "Was that close?" replaces fear. Not bravery—adaptation for function.
</A6_siege>
entries.name: #C1 Siege & Blockade Living

entries.content:
<A6_warlife>
CIVILIAN WARTIME DAILY LIFE:

DAILY RHYTHM AROUND VIOLENCE:
- Shelling patterns exist. Residents learn: "mornings quiet, afternoons dangerous, nights worst."
- "Safe" windows used for: water collection, food search, moving between buildings.
- Pattern changes without warning. "Safe" hour becomes fatal.

SHELTER CULTURE:
- Basement/underground parking becomes home for days-weeks.
- Social hierarchy forms: who has supplies, who has information, who has children, who is sick.
- Conflict inside shelter: space, noise, hygiene, food distribution.
- No privacy. Bodily functions, grief, arguments—all witnessed.

CHILDREN:
- Adapt faster than adults expect. Play between shelling. Normalize sirens.
- School stops. Education gap begins immediately.
- Trauma appears later, not during. During = survival mode.

FOOD/WATER:
- Cooking requires fuel (gas, wood) and safety window. Quick meals, cold meals.
- Bakeries become lifelines and targets. Standing in bread line = risk calculation.

COMMUNICATION:
- Power for phone charging = precious. Charging stations become community gathering points.
- Who is alive, who isn't: information spreads through networks, not news. Confirmed by who shows up today.
</A6_warlife>
entries.name: #C2 Civilian Wartime Daily Life

entries.content:
<A6_refugee>
DISPLACEMENT & REFUGEE MECHANICS:

DOCUMENTATION:
- Fled without documents = cannot prove identity. Cannot work, rent, access services legally.
- Documents from collapsed/unrecognized state = worthless. Professional credentials unverifiable.
- Children born in displacement: statelessness risk.

JOURNEY:
- Smugglers: paid thousands for dangerous passage. No guarantee. Exploitation during transit.
- Physical: walking days, boats, trucks, exposure, dehydration. Children and elderly die en route.
- Borders: closed, or open with conditions no one meets.

CAMP CONDITIONS:
- Designed temporary, last decades. Tents → shanties → semi-permanent settlement.
- Overcrowding, shared sanitation, limited water, disease outbreaks.
- Power dynamics: camp leadership, aid distribution politics, gender-based violence.
- Waiting: for processing, resettlement, return. Months become years. Life suspended.

IDENTITY EROSION:
- Doctor, teacher, engineer → "refugee" as sole identity. Skills irrelevant without recognition.
- Language barrier: children learn new language faster than parents. Family hierarchy inverts.
- Community: displaced groups cluster. Recreate home culture in exile. Isolation from host population.
</A6_refugee>
entries.name: #C3 Displacement & Refugee Mechanics

entries.content:
<A6_occupy>
OCCUPATION & CONTROL:

CHECKPOINT DAILY LIFE:
- Queue for hours to cross distance that took minutes before.
- Arbitrary: same checkpoint, different soldier, different rules each day.
- Humiliation is feature not bug: ID checks at gunpoint, bags emptied on ground, waiting in sun/rain.
- Refusal or complaint = detained. Duration unknown.

PERMIT SYSTEM:
- Need permit for: work, travel, medical access, building, farming, water access.
- Permits denied without reason. Application itself is risk (now you're in the system).
- Life organized around what permits allow. Not what person needs.

INFORMATION CONTROL:
- Internet shutdowns during protests/operations. Routine, not exceptional.
- Journalists restricted. Local reporting = personal risk.
- Official narrative and ground reality are parallel universes.

DAILY REALITY:
- Not constant violence. Mostly: restriction, uncertainty, arbitrary authority, erosion of dignity.
- Night raids: military enters homes at 3AM. Searches. Takes someone. Family may not know destination.
- Normalization: children grow up knowing checkpoint procedure. It's their normal.

RESISTANCE vs SURVIVAL:
- Not binary. Same person cooperates at checkpoint and supports resistance at home.
- Collaboration is survival strategy, not character flaw. Judging from outside is easy.
</A6_occupy>
entries.name: #C4 Occupation & Control

entries.content:
<A6_resctrl>
RESOURCE CONTROL AS GOVERNANCE:

HOW IT WORKS:
- Water, electricity, fuel, medical supply, internet—each is a control lever.
- Not always total cutoff. Reduced supply, unpredictable schedule, conditional access. Dependency maintained.
- "We didn't cut it off. The infrastructure failed." Plausible deniability by neglect.

BUREAUCRATIC CONTROL:
- Legal framework that excludes by design: visa requirements impossible to meet, permits with undisclosed criteria.
- Not one dramatic law. Hundreds of small regulations that individually seem reasonable but collectively strangle.
- Challenging any single rule = "the process is fair." Challenging the system = "that's conspiracy thinking."

ECONOMIC STRANGULATION:
- Not dramatic embargo. Slow restriction: tariffs, banking access, import licenses, currency controls.
- Businesses close one by one. Employment disappears. Dependency on whoever controls remaining resources.

GRADUAL vs SUDDEN:
- Sudden cutoff = international attention, outrage, response.
- Gradual degradation = "things are just hard." No dramatic moment. No clear villain. No intervention trigger.
- Most effective control is the kind that doesn't look like control.
</A6_resctrl>
entries.name: #S1 Resource Control as Governance

entries.content:
<A6_infoctrl>
INFORMATION & NARRATIVE CONTROL:

WHO TELLS THE STORY:
- Access determines narrative. No journalists in = no coverage = didn't happen.
- Language barrier: local voices exist but need translation to reach international audience. Translator = filter.
- Platform access: whose internet works, whose social media reaches outside.

FRAMING:
- "Conflict between two sides" = false equivalence when power is asymmetric.
- "Complicated situation" = permission to disengage.
- Passive voice: "people died" vs "forces killed people." Grammar is politics.

SOCIAL MEDIA:
- Lifeline: real-time documentation, bypasses traditional media gatekeepers.
- Weapon: coordinated disinformation campaigns, bot networks, hashtag hijacking.
- Platform decisions (content moderation, algorithm, verification) shape which reality is visible.

CENSORSHIP SPECTRUM:
- Direct: banned topics, jailed journalists, removed content.
- Indirect: flooding zone with noise so signal drowns. Discrediting rather than silencing.
- Self-censorship: most effective. People stop talking because consequences are known. No enforcement needed.

PROPAGANDA:
- Effective propaganda contains enough truth to be believable. Pure fabrication is amateur.
- Repetition > evidence. Repeated claim becomes "what everyone knows."
</A6_infoctrl>
entries.name: #S2 Information & Narrative Control

entries.content:
<A5_consent>
[PHYSIOLOGY: AROUSAL-BODY DISCONNECT]
[CRITICAL — CONSENT-RELEVANT]

PHYSICAL AROUSAL ≠ DESIRE OR CONSENT.

GENITAL RESPONSE IS AUTONOMIC:
- Erection can occur from fear, friction, or random stimulus. Does not mean "wants it."
- Vaginal lubrication can occur from physical stimulation alone. Does not mean "enjoys it."
- Nipple erection responds to temperature, touch, hormones. Not exclusively sexual.

THIS MEANS:
- "But you're wet/hard" is NOT valid evidence of desire
- Bodies respond to stimulation mechanically; brain consent is separate system
- Arousal during unwanted contact = normal physiological response, NOT indicator of hidden desire
- Survivors often experience confusion/shame about physical response during assault

IN FICTION/RP:
- Character may experience physical arousal while emotionally conflicted, frightened, or unwilling
- Narrate this as distressing contradiction, not "secret enjoyment"
- Other characters interpreting arousal as consent = that character being wrong, not narrative truth

CONSENT ROUTE: Treat wetness/erection as autonomic body data. Desire comes from communicated willingness; unwanted arousal reads as distressing contradiction, never "body is honest."
</A5_consent>
entries.name: #PH5 Arousal-Body Disconnect

entries.content:
<A5_forgasm>
[PHYSIOLOGY: FEMALE ORGASM]

CORE FACT: Most vulva-havers do not orgasm from penetration alone.

ORGASM TYPES (not hierarchy—different pathways, not "levels"):
- Clitoral: most common, most reliable. Direct or indirect stimulation.
- Vaginal/G-spot: minority experience this. Requires specific angle, pressure, arousal level.
- Blended: clitoral + penetrative simultaneously. Not default.
- No orgasm: possible outcome even with arousal and enjoyment. Not failure.

INDIVIDUAL VARIANCE:
- Some orgasm easily, some rarely, some never have
- Consistent method ≠ universal method
- What worked last time may not work this time
- Mental state (stress, distraction, pressure to perform) directly affects ability

MULTIPLE ORGASMS:
- Possible for some, not all
- No universal refractory period, but sensitivity/fatigue accumulates
- Sequential ≠ effortless; each may require rebuilding arousal
- Diminishing intensity common after 2-3

SIMULTANEOUS ORGASM:
- Rare coincidence, not expected outcome
- Attempting to sync often disrupts both
- Porn convention, not physiological norm

ORGASM ROUTE: Use clitoral involvement as the reliable default. Penetration-only orgasm needs an established character-specific pattern.
</A5_forgasm>
entries.name: #PH1 Female Orgasm Physiology

entries.content:
<A5_lube>
[PHYSIOLOGY: AROUSAL & LUBRICATION]

LUBRICATION ≠ AROUSAL LEVEL:
- Abundant fluid can occur with minimal arousal; minimal fluid can occur during intense arousal.
- Medication, hormonal BC, HRT, menopause, cycle phase, hydration, stress, fatigue, and age all shift production.

INSUFFICIENT LUBRICATION:
Common, neutral, and not partner failure. Friction without lubrication causes microtears, pain, and infection risk. External lubricant is a tool, not consolation.

EXCESS LUBRICATION:
May reduce friction or sensation. Wiping with a towel is a valid adjustment. High wetness is not a promiscuity signal.

AROUSAL TIMELINE:
Clitoral/labial engorgement takes minutes. Lubrication may lag behind subjective desire. Penetration before body readiness causes pain even when desire is present.

READINESS ROUTE:
Vulva arousal is not always visually obvious. Erection and lubrication are different signals. Write checking in, observed comfort, pacing, and adjustment instead of using wetness as universal proof of readiness.
</A5_lube>
entries.name: #PH3 Arousal & Lubrication Variance

entries.content:
<A5_morgasm>
[PHYSIOLOGY: PENIS ORGASM & REFRACTORY]

ORGASM ≠ EJACULATION:
Usually concurrent, sometimes separate. Dry orgasm can occur through practice, prostate stimulation, vasectomy, or HRT context. Ejaculation can happen without full orgasmic satisfaction.

REFRACTORY PERIOD:
After ejaculation, erection typically fades and further stimulation may feel uncomfortable. Recovery ranges from minutes to hours by individual, age, fatigue, hydration, and arousal context. During refractory, hypersensitivity and low responsiveness are normal.

PREMATURE EJACULATION:
Common, not character flaw. Routes: overstimulation, anxiety, inexperience, long abstinence, high sensitivity. Management: pacing, stop-start, changing stimulation, practice.

DELAYED/ABSENT EJACULATION:
Also common. Causes include SSRIs, anxiety, fatigue, death-grip conditioning. Extended vigorous thrusting to force finish creates pain and frustration.

MULTIPLE ORGASMS (penis-havers):
Possible for some when orgasm separates from ejaculation, but not baseline. Most have one orgasm followed by refractory management.
</A5_morgasm>
entries.name: #PH4 Male/Penis Orgasm & Refractory

entries.content:
<A5_ejac>
[PHYSIOLOGY: EJACULATION & SQUIRTING]

SQUIRTING:
Not universal and not technique-guaranteed. It is not proof of better orgasm or higher arousal. Fluid is usually dilute urine plus Skene's gland secretions. Volume is often small; high-volume fountains are porn exaggeration for most. Squirting can occur without orgasm; orgasm can occur without squirting.

PENILE EJACULATION:
Average volume is 1-5ml, roughly a teaspoon. Distance ranges from dribble to short arc. Repeated ejaculations reduce force and volume. Pre-ejaculate is clear, small volume, and may contain sperm.

GOCK (HRT):
Estrogen often reduces or stops ejaculate volume. Orgasm can remain present and may be dry or differently patterned.

CLEANUP REALITY:
Squirting may need towels and sheet protection. Ejaculate is small cleanup and dries sticky. Write it as manageable body reality, not cinematic spectacle or satisfaction score.
</A5_ejac>
entries.name: #PH2 Ejaculation & Squirting Realism

entries.content:
<A5_erogenous>
[PHYSIOLOGY: EROGENOUS ZONE INDIVIDUALITY]

NO UNIVERSAL SENSITIVITY MAP.

COMMON ZONES VARY:
Nipples may feel intense or almost blank. Neck can be erotic, ticklish, or irritating. Ears may arouse or disgust. Inner thigh can be neutral, ticklish, or sensitive. Clitoral preference varies: indirect, direct, soft, firm, rhythmic, or changing by mood.

UNCOMMON ZONES CAN MATTER:
Scalp, lower back/sacrum, behind knees, wrists/inner forearm, collarbone hollow, hip bones, feet. For one person: electric. For another: nothing or tickle-only.

DISCOVERY IS COMMUNICATION:
Partners learn maps through feedback, breath, flinch, leaning in, verbal check-ins, and adjustment. Asking "does this feel good?" is competence. Hormones, age, mood, trust, fatigue, and cycle phase can change the map over time.

TICKLISH ≠ EROGENOUS:
Shared nerve pathways, different response. Light touch may trigger involuntary flinch. Firmer pressure may bypass tickle into pleasure, or fail. Derive sensitivity from profile or discover it in-scene.
</A5_erogenous>
entries.name: #PH6 Erogenous Zone Individuality

entries.content:
<A5_config>
Anatomical configuration determines penetration mechanics and stimulation targets.

VULVA + VULVA (no tool):
- Tribbing: direct vulva contact, alignment matters for clitoral stimulation
- Grinding: thigh, hip, pubic bone as friction surface
- Penetration requires hands/fingers or external tool

VULVA + VULVA (with tool):
- Strap-on: wearer has no direct penetrative sensation; base may provide indirect pressure
- Double-ended: both receive penetration; coordination required; neither has full control
- Handheld: one partner controls depth/angle for other

VULVA + PENIS/GOCK:
- Penetration angle affects G-spot vs depth stimulation
- Gock (HRT): may have altered erection pattern, softer, sensation differs—direct communication essential

ANAL ACCESS (any configuration):
- External prostate stimulation possible for those with prostates
- Universal considerations: lube mandatory, warmup required, different angle than vaginal

ANATOMY-CONDITIONAL (mandatory):
- No prostate language for vulva-owners. No "her prostate," no prostate orgasm, no prostate struck.
- Anal pleasure without a prostate comes from pelvic floor mechanics, pudendal innervation, tissue displacement, and indirect pressure on the internal clitoral complex. Not a prostate analogue.
- The anterior wall is not "less sensitive." Which structures respond is individual.
</A5_config>
entries.name: #M5 Anatomical Configuration

entries.content:
<A5_disadapt>
Physical disability modifies position selection and execution. Adaptation is logistics, not limitation.

UPPER LIMB DIFFERENCE:
- Single arm/hand: positions requiring bilateral arm support (pushup-style missionary, planks) require modification—forearm support, partner assists weight, pillows
- Prosthetic: may remove for comfort/sensation; residual limb sensitivity varies (some erogenous, some painful)
- Grip strength affected: alternatives to grabbing (hooking elbow, using body weight)

LOWER LIMB DIFFERENCE:
- Single leg/limited mobility: positions requiring leg wrap or spread adapt—pillows for support, partner holds leg position
- Wheelchair user: chair itself becomes furniture—seated positions, edge-of-chair, transfers to bed with planning

CHRONIC PAIN (back, joints):
- Avoid strain positions for affected area
- Spooning, side-lying, supported seated = lower impact
- Pillows are tools, not optional

DOM with disability: dominance is psychological and positional, not dependent on physical wholeness. Control through voice, positioning, restraints, directing partner's body.

Adaptation is planned, not improvised mid-act. Discuss before.
</A5_disadapt>
entries.name: #M2 Disability Adaptation

entries.content:
<A5_overstim>
[MODIFIER: SENSITIVITY & OVERSTIMULATION]

EROGENOUS ZONES HAVE LIMITS:

CLITORIS:
- Highly concentrated nerve endings (8000+)
- Direct sustained stimulation: pleasurable → intense → uncomfortable → painful
- Post-orgasm: often HYPER-sensitive; continued direct contact = sharp discomfort or pain

IMMEDIATE POST-ACTIVITY:

- Collapsing in place: common, valid
- Gradual position shift as breathing normalizes

- Spooning: warmth, full-body contact, one person "held"
